articles.title: How much money is considered rich?
articles.summary: What does it mean to be rich in America? The answer isn't the same for everyone. Here are some common measures of wealth, plus some tips for growing yours.
articles.body:

What does it really mean to be rich? For some, it's earning a six-figure salary. For others, it's having enough money saved to never work again. But while the definition of wealth is subjective, there are some concrete numbers that can help put it into perspective.

What is considered 'rich' in America today?

In the United States, there are certainly people who we can consider rich by every conceivable measure (certain tech CEOs may come to mind). However, it may not require a massive net worth to be considered rich by most people.

According to a survey from Charles Schwab, Americans believe an average net worth of $2.3 million is necessary to be considered rich.

That said, whether or not a person is rich is relative to their situation.

For example, let's say you earn a salary of $208,152 per year, which puts you squarely within the top 10% of U.S. wage earners, according to ZipRecruiter.

You might say earning that salary — which is more than three times what the average U.S. worker earns — makes you rich since it allows you to easily afford the median-priced home in most parts of the country. But that salary is still not enough to afford the median-priced home in Massachusetts, Hawaii, or California, according to Realtor.com.

Plus, even if you do earn around $200,000 per year, other factors such as your debt, job security, family size, and medical expenses can determine if you're truly financially stable — not to mention whether or not you're happy.

Speaking of happiness, the amount of money it takes to make us happy varies, too. But it's an easier goal to obtain than being rich. According to a study from the University of Pennsylvania, happiness increases for most people as their income increases, but it plateaus once they reach $100,000 per year.

There's no one road that leads to wealth, but there are basic principles you can follow to make an easier path. Here are some things you can do to kick-start the journey.

Many people in the U.S. incorrectly believe that their inheritance is too small to fuss over and that estate planning is for the ultra-wealthy. But the truth is that a lack of estate planning among lower-income groups can contribute to ongoing wealth disparities.

One of the main ways to increase your wealth is by strategically planning for the transfer of assets you'll inherit. For one, that inheritance is taxed at a far lower rate than money earned by working or saving. In other words, estate planning can give you a better opportunity to increase your net worth aside from just working.

So if you believe you will have any inheritance at all, talk to a certified financial planner to see how you can avoid unnecessary delays and taxes that will reduce what's transferred to you.

If you want to easily afford all of your needs, it may require a bigger lifestyle change. You may want to consider moving to a location where the cost of living is lower than where you currently reside, but where you can still maintain or even increase your income.

By doing so, you not only have the potential to cut your cost of living by as much as 50% or more, but you can also free up more of your income to invest and earn passive income .

Financial experts often advise people to tighten their budgets in order to improve their finances. But that's not the only way to make improvements. In fact, budgeting can only get you so far if your income is limited.

By contrast, you can often make a much bigger impact if you proactively look for ways to increase your income on a regular and ongoing basis.

How do you do this? Despite what you may have heard, attending college is still one of the best ways to ensure you'll earn the highest income possible.

According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, people who obtain a bachelor's degree or higher earn significantly more than those who only graduate high school or even those who obtain an associate degree.

After college, you can see a huge difference in your income trajectory if you look for ways to increase your pay annually.

For example, if your first professional role pays $75,000 a year and you receive the average annual pay raise (3%), your income won't keep up with inflation. After five years, your salary will only increase to $86,946.

By comparison, human resources management software and services provider ADP estimates that people who switch jobs increase their income by around 7% (which is low compared to recent years). At that rate, if you were currently earning $75,000 and switched jobs right away, your salary would increase to $80,250 this year. Then, if you negotiated a 5% increase each year thereafter, your income would reach $97,544 in five years.

One of the fastest ways to lose money is to use credit cards and take on other high-interest debt. That's because you're unlikely to find any investment that earns higher interest rates than what you're charged on credit card debt; the average credit card APR hovers around 22%, while you can expect to earn roughly 7% to 10% from long-term stock market investments.

There's a limit to how much you can earn when you exchange your labor for pay, also known as earning active income. If you want to increase your earning power, focus on developing additional, passive forms of income, or income that's earned by putting your assets to work.

The sooner you pay off debt and start investing your money, the more time your money has to grow and multiply.

That's because of a principle called compound interest . With compound interest, you earn money not just on the amount you invest, but also on the interest you've earned to date. So the longer your money is invested, the more its value can grow.

Some people take this to mean that there's no point in investing at a later age. On the contrary, it simply means the sooner you start, the better. If you leave your surplus cash in the bank, for example, it won't usually earn enough interest to keep up with inflation . On the other hand, investing in a diverse portfolio of stocks, mutual funds, bonds, and other securities can allow you to beat inflation and grow your net worth , regardless of your age.

articles.title: Why Dell (DELL) shares are getting obliterated today
articles.summary: Shares of computer hardware and IT solutions company Dell (NYSE:DELL) fell 9.5% in the morning session after Intel warned of a prolonged slump in personal co...
articles.body:
Shares of computer hardware and IT solutions company Dell (NYSE:DELL) fell 9.5% in the morning session after Intel warned of a prolonged slump in personal computer demand and forecast steep declines in global shipments.

In prepared remarks accompanying its earnings results, Intel Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan projected global personal computer shipments to decline 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027, driven by component shortages and increasing memory prices. Tan explained that the market correction accelerated over the previous two months as original equipment manufacturing partners reduced inventories, warning that the slump could persist through the first half of 2027 until component pricing stabilizes.

Notably, preliminary industry figures released from research firms IDC and Counterpoint Research indicated third-quarter global PC shipments fell between 20.1% and 21% year-over-year, which included a 25% plunge for Dell. The severe contraction highlights vulnerability to cyclical downturns in hardware demand and rising component expenses.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy Dell? Access our full analysis report here, it's free .

Dell's shares are extremely volatile and have had 47 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock gained 8.3% on the news that the company announced an expansion of its cybersecurity and resilience portfolio for artificial intelligence environments and introduced new personal computers designed for AI.

According to Dell's press release, the new services cover AI systems, identity platforms, and storage. Security Hardening for the Dell AI Factory, available this month, reviews the physical, virtual, and application layers of an AI deployment and ranks the configuration risks. Resilience Operations for AI, available now, identifies the AI applications a customer has to keep running and writes the recovery plan. PowerProtect identity tools, available now, restore a clean copy of Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and Okta after an attack.These additions strengthen Dell's position in enterprise infrastructure and software, addressing heightened corporate focus on securing AI deployments and critical corporate identities.

articles.title: Madeira, esterco e lodo de esgoto são transformados em fertilizantes e movimentam economia circular | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Marilândia, distrito de Itapecerica, no Centro-Oeste de Minas Gerais, os resíduos se tornam adubo de qualidade, movimentando a economia e impulsionando a sustentabilidade.
articles.summary: Em  Marilândia, distrito de Itapecerica, no Centro-Oeste de Minas Gerais, os resíduos se tornam adubo de qualidade, movimentando a economia e impulsionando a sustentabilidade.
articles.body:
Em Marilândia, distrito de Itapecerica , no Centro-Oeste de Minas Gerais, cascas de eucalipto, restos de madeira, serraria, podas urbanas, estercos e lodo de tratamento de esgoto estão sendo transformados em fertilizante orgânico e reduzindo custos de produtores rurais.

Segundo o empresário e engenheiro florestal Renato Gatti, o adubo orgânico é produto de uma mistura que passa pela ativação de microrganismos. Todo o processo pode demorar até 120 dias.

"Quando recebemos esses resíduos, eles são misturados e com a ativação de alguns microrganismos que nós multiplicamos on farm, eles aceleram todo o processo de decomposição. Eles são enleirados, mantemos temperatura e umidade controlados para criar o melhor ambiente decompositor possível. E após um período de 60 a 120 dias temos a leira pronta para ser aberta peneirada", disse Gatti.

🔎 On farm - expressão em inglês que significa "na fazenda" - é a produção de bioinsumos e microrganismos benéficos — como bactérias e fungos — diretamente dentro da propriedade rural.

🔎 Leirar é o processo de juntar os materiais em linhas uniformes chamadas leiras.

Economia circular: produção de fertilizantes orgânicos ganha força no Centro-Oeste mineiro — Foto: TV Integração/Reprodução

O empresário afirmou que a iniciativa tem transformado a gestão de resíduos, o futuro da produção agrícola e se transformou em um elo vital da economia circular na região.

"Toda aquela teoria de ESG e economia circular, a gente vê ela aqui na prática. Recebemos resíduos de algumas indústrias, sejam granjas ou alimentícias, que nos encaminham esses resíduos que anteriormente eram destinados para aterros e aqui são transformados em um adubo riquíssimo, que vai fomentar de novo produtores de cereais, que são a base para as rações dos animais", finalizou Renato Gatti.

A empresa, que opera desde 2020, tem produção anual de 15 mil toneladas.

Adubo orgânico ganha espaço em propriedades rurais

A busca por maior eficiência produtiva e a necessidade de reduzir gastos têm levado produtores a adotarem o adubo orgânico. Exemplo disso é a fazenda de Álvaro Franccino, que cultiva soja, milho e feijão em 500 hectares em Monsenhor João Alexandre, distrito de Cláudio.

Há dois anos, o produtor iniciou a transição do adubo convencional para o orgânico após observar resultados positivos em outras regiões.

Atualmente, a propriedade trabalha com uma divisão equilibrada: 50% de adubo convencional e 50% orgânico. No entanto, a meta é atingir 100% de uso de adubo orgânico em um prazo de cinco anos.

"A gente quer transferir a produção para a própria fazenda. Não queremos comprar nada de fora no prazo de cinco anos", afirma o produtor.

O incentivo para a mudança é claro: a expectativa é alcançar uma economia de 50% nos custos totais com fertilizantes.

articles.title: Polymarket e Kalshi: por que apostas sobre as eleições preocupam especialistas nos EUA? | G1
articles.standfirst: Plataformas ganharam espaço na cobertura eleitoral dos EUA, mas especialistas alertam que suas estimativas podem ser confundidas com resultados garantidos e alimentar acusações infundadas de fraude.
articles.summary: Plataformas ganharam espaço na cobertura eleitoral dos EUA, mas especialistas alertam que suas estimativas podem ser confundidas com resultados garantidos e alimentar acusações infundadas de fraude.
articles.body:
Midterms - Eleitora preenche cédula de votação em Harrisburg, na Pensilvânia (EUA) — Foto: REUTERS/Mike Segar

As eleições legislativas dos Estados Unidos acontecem em um momento de expansão dos chamados mercados de previsão , plataformas nas quais os usuários podem apostar dinheiro em possíveis resultados de acontecimentos, incluindo disputas eleitorais.

O uso dessas plataformas em eleições, porém, preocupa especialistas pelo risco de disseminação de informações falsas e de interpretações equivocadas sobre os resultados das urnas.

Especialistas alertam que os percentuais exibidos nessas plataformas podem ser interpretados como resultados praticamente garantidos, embora representem apenas estimativas. Há também situações em que grupos políticos tentam influenciar essas probabilidades.

Se o resultado das urnas for diferente do indicado pelos mercados de previsão, alguns eleitores podem interpretar essa divergência como indício de fraude, mesmo que ela não represente uma irregularidade.

Plataformas como Polymarket e Kalshi permitem que usuários negociem contratos cujo valor depende de resultados eleitorais. Apesar do crescimento desse mercado, pesquisas indicam que a maioria dos americanos é contrária à realização de apostas sobre eleições.

🚫 No Brasil, a oferta de contratos vinculados a resultados eleitorais está proibida desde maio de 2026. Uma resolução do Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN) passou a impedir operações financeiras relacionadas a acontecimentos políticos e eleitorais, além de outros eventos sem ligação com indicadores econômicos e financeiros. A medida também levou ao bloqueio de plataformas como Polymarket e Kalshi no país.

As probabilidades divulgadas pelas duas plataformas também passaram a aparecer na cobertura de grandes veículos de comunicação, ampliando a presença dos mercados de previsão no noticiário eleitoral.

"Elas se tornaram cada vez mais parte de como os americanos entendem as eleições", diz Davina Hurt, diretora de ética governamental do Centro Markkula de Ética Aplicada da Universidade de Santa Clara.

"Estamos chegando a um ponto em que as expectativas dos mercados financeiros têm mais peso na mente do público do que os votos", acrescenta.

Os mercados de previsão estão se popularizando nos EUA, mas ainda enfrentam disputas judiciais sobre quais regras devem seguir. A discussão é se essas plataformas devem ser reguladas como mercados de commodities, que negociam determinados ativos e contratos, ou se devem estar sujeitas às leis sobre apostas.

A Kalshi afirma que as informações oferecidas por sua plataforma são diferentes das apresentadas pelas pesquisas eleitorais tradicionais. A empresa reconhece, porém, que as probabilidades divulgadas não garantem que determinado resultado vá se concretizar.

Segundo a companhia, eventuais tentativas de manipular as probabilidades tendem a ser compensadas pelas negociações realizadas por outros usuários da plataforma.

"A Kalshi deve ser vista como um complemento às pesquisas tradicionais", disse à AFP Elisabeth Diana, diretora de comunicação da plataforma.

Apesar dessas explicações, especialistas alertam que os percentuais podem ser confundidos com resultados já definidos. O risco aumenta porque Polymarket e Kalshi também divulgam suas estimativas nas redes sociais, ampliando o alcance dessas informações.

Hurt ressalta que, mesmo quando uma plataforma aponta uma probabilidade elevada, isso não significa que o resultado esteja garantido.

"Uma alta probabilidade não é uma promessa (...) Quando uma previsão acaba se revelando errada, isso não significa que a escolha tenha sido equivocada. No entanto, as pessoas vão interpretar dessa maneira", diz Hurt.

Derrota em Los Angeles provoca acusações de fraude

Um episódio ocorrido em junho, nas eleições primárias para a Prefeitura de Los Angeles, mostrou como as probabilidades dos mercados podem ser confundidas com os resultados das urnas.

Após a derrota do republicano Spencer Pratt, influenciadores de direita fizeram acusações de fraude, citando estimativas das plataformas que indicavam chances de o candidato avançar para a eleição geral.

Parte das publicações com informações falsas na rede social X aparecia identificada como "parceria paga". O episódio provocou críticas e levou Polymarket e Kalshi a adotar medidas em relação à divulgação desse tipo de conteúdo.

"A primária de junho mostrou como as expectativas sobre uma eleição podem ser confundidas com os resultados", disse Michael Sánchez, porta-voz do Escritório de Registro Eleitoral do Condado de Los Angeles.

Em um documento obtido com exclusividade pela agência AFP, a Kalshi orientou seus parceiros a não questionar resultados eleitorais oficiais sem apresentar fundamentos para isso.

Segundo o documento, os parceiros "não devem questionar a integridade nem a precisão de nenhum resultado oficial da contagem de votos, decisão judicial ou outra determinação oficial ou formal ligada ao processo eleitoral".

A empresa também afirmou que romperá contratos com parceiros que fizerem acusações sem provas de "que um resultado eleitoral foi manipulado, fraudado ou comprometido".

A Polymarket não respondeu aos pedidos de comentário.

Autoridade eleitoral questiona regras para apostas

O avanço dos mercados de previsão também preocupa autoridades eleitorais. Jared DeMarinis, responsável pela administração das eleições no estado de Maryland, pediu uma avaliação sobre a legalidade das apostas relacionadas a disputas eleitorais no estado.

Em entrevista à AFP, DeMarinis afirmou que proibiu os mesários de apostar em resultados eleitorais.

"Agora simplesmente se jogou mais gasolina ao envolver dinheiro nisso. O que menos se quer é que se coloque em dúvida a legitimidade do resultado", afirmou.

articles.title: Acordo Mercosul-UE: agro exporta 14,8% mais em seis meses | G1
articles.standfirst: Vendas ao bloco europeu somaram US$ 12,21 bilhões entre maio e setembro de 2026. Soja, carnes, mel e frutas puxaram o crescimento, segundo o Ministério da Agricultura.
articles.summary: Vendas ao bloco europeu somaram US$ 12,21 bilhões entre maio e setembro de 2026. Soja, carnes, mel e frutas puxaram o crescimento, segundo o Ministério da Agricultura.
articles.body:
Porto com contêineres para exportação — Foto: Divulgação

Depois de mais de 25 anos de negociações, o acordo comercial entre o Mercosul e a União Europeia começou a produzir efeitos em maio deste ano , abrindo caminho para a redução de tarifas e ampliando as oportunidades de exportação para empresas brasileiras.

A parceria conecta dois grandes mercados, que juntos reúnem cerca de 720 milhões de pessoas e têm um Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) superior a US$ 22 trilhões.

Os primeiros resultados já mostram crescimento nas vendas de produtos brasileiros beneficiados pelo tratado.

Nos cinco primeiros meses de aplicação provisória, as exportações desses itens para a União Europeia avançaram 21% , considerando diferentes setores da economia, de acordo com o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC).

No agronegócio, o avanço foi de 14,8% em valor . As vendas brasileiras de produtos agropecuários e agroindustriais ao bloco europeu somaram US$ 12,21 bilhões entre maio e setembro de 2026, na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado, segundo dados do Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária (Mapa).

🔎 Na prática, por que as exportações estão crescendo? Com a redução das tarifas de importação, produtos brasileiros ficam mais competitivos no mercado europeu, o que facilita a entrada e amplia as oportunidades de venda.

O acordo completa seis meses neste domingo (1º). No período analisado, o Brasil embarcou 17,74 milhões de toneladas de produtos do agronegócio para os 27 países da União Europeia, volume 8,1% superior ao registrado nos mesmos meses de 2025.

O crescimento foi puxado por diferentes segmentos, como mel, carnes, soja e frutas . Entre os produtos individuais, o abacate e o óleo de milho tiveram algumas das maiores altas percentuais.

Embora o agronegócio seja um dos setores beneficiados, o avanço das exportações também alcançou a indústria. Entre os produtos com crescimento nas vendas estão ferrossilício-manganês, alumínio em bruto, óleos combustíveis e etanol. As exportações de transformadores elétricos, por exemplo, passaram de zero para US$ 39 milhões no período analisado.

Veja quais setores do agronegócio tiveram maior crescimento

Os produtos apícolas, principalmente o mel, registraram a maior alta percentual entre os segmentos destacados pelo Ministério da Agricultura: 367% em valor.

Na sequência, aparecem os produtos oleaginosos, exceto soja, com crescimento de 161%. As exportações de carnes avançaram 103,5% em valor e 170% em volume, passando de 101 mil toneladas para 272 mil toneladas.

Outros segmentos também tiveram desempenho positivo:

Complexo soja: alta de 34,2% em valor, de US$ 3,12 bilhões para US$ 4,19 bilhões;

Produtos florestais: crescimento de 23%, de US$ 1,2 bilhão para US$ 1,48 bilhão;

Frutas, nozes e castanhas: avanço de 15%, de US$ 274 milhões para US$ 315 milhões;

Demais produtos de origem animal: aumento de 55,5% em valor.

Apesar das altas expressivas em outros segmentos, o complexo soja permaneceu como o principal grupo de produtos exportados pelo agronegócio brasileiro para a União Europeia.

Dentro desse segmento, as vendas de soja em grãos cresceram 49% em valor e 35,1% em volume. Já as exportações de farelo de soja avançaram 22,5% em valor e 10,6% em volume.

Abacate e óleo de milho se destacam entre produtos individuais

🥑 Entre os produtos individuais, o abacate teve uma das maiores expansões percentuais. As exportações passaram de US$ 3,81 milhões, entre maio e setembro de 2025, para US$ 19,87 milhões no mesmo período de 2026, alta de 421,2%.

O volume embarcado também aumentou: 433,7%.

Outro destaque foi o óleo de milho bruto, cujas vendas cresceram 266,3% em valor, passando de US$ 35,31 milhões para US$ 129,35 milhões. Em volume, a alta foi de 205,8%.

Outras frutas também ampliaram as vendas ao mercado europeu. As exportações de manga cresceram 31,2% em valor e 23,6% em volume. As de maçã avançaram 28,8% em valor e 33,7% em volume.

No setor cafeeiro, as vendas de café torrado tiveram alta de 91,6% em valor e 116,5% em volume. Já as exportações de café solúvel cresceram 19% em valor e 38,2% em volume.

Acordo prevê redução de tarifas para produtos brasileiros

A aplicação provisória das regras comerciais do acordo começou em 1º de maio de 2026. Desde então, determinados produtos agropecuários brasileiros passaram a contar com reduções tarifárias para entrar no mercado europeu, conforme os cronogramas negociados entre os dois blocos.

Entre os produtos beneficiados estão o café torrado, o café solúvel e o abacate.

Para os dois tipos de café, a redução das tarifas será gradual, com previsão de eliminação completa em 2030. No caso do abacate, o primeiro corte correspondeu a 20% da tarifa-base, com liberalização total também prevista para 2030.

O acordo prevê ainda condições de acesso ao mercado europeu para outros produtos importantes da pauta exportadora brasileira, como carnes bovina, suína e de aves, açúcar, etanol, arroz, mel, milho e sorgo.

Em alguns casos, os benefícios estão vinculados a cotas de importação, com limites de volume e condições específicas para cada produto.

Brasil mantém superávit no comércio agropecuário com a UE

As importações brasileiras de produtos agropecuários e agroindustriais provenientes da União Europeia somaram US$ 1,67 bilhão entre maio e setembro de 2026, alta de 3,3% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025, quando chegaram a US$ 1,62 bilhão.

Mesmo com o aumento das compras, o Brasil ampliou o superávit comercial do agronegócio com o bloco europeu.

O saldo positivo passou de US$ 9,01 bilhões nos cinco primeiros meses de 2025 para US$ 10,54 bilhões em 2026, crescimento de 17%.

Negociações duraram mais de duas décadas

As negociações entre Mercosul e União Europeia começaram em 1999 e se estenderam por mais de 25 anos.

Ao longo desse período, divergências comerciais, ambientais e políticas dificultaram a conclusão do tratado.

Os instrumentos do acordo foram assinados em 17 de janeiro de 2026. A aplicação provisória das disposições comerciais começou em 1º de maio, permitindo que parte dos compromissos de redução tarifária passasse a valer antes da entrada em vigor definitiva da parceria.

O acordo prevê a liberalização total ou parcial de aproximadamente 99% das exportações agrícolas brasileiras para o mercado europeu, por meio da eliminação de tarifas ou de condições preferenciais de acesso, incluindo cotas para determinados produtos.

A implementação, no entanto, está sendo gradual. Além de aproveitar as condições tarifárias, os exportadores brasileiros precisam cumprir exigências sanitárias, ambientais e de rastreabilidade estabelecidas pela União Europeia.

➡️ Entre os pontos de atenção está o Regulamento da União Europeia sobre Produtos Livres de Desmatamento (EUDR), que estabelece requisitos ambientais para a entrada de determinadas mercadorias no bloco.

articles.title: Expedicionários da Saúde iniciam projeto de 4 anos no Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa tem apoio do Fundo Amazônia. Cerca de 60 profissionais oferecem atendimentos de oftalmologia, cirurgia geral, pediatria e saúde da mulher.
articles.summary: Os Expedicionários da Saúde iniciam o projeto Cuidar para Preservar no Amazonas, levando cirurgias e exames especializados a indígenas do Alto Rio Negro.
articles.body:
Expedicionários da Saúde voltam a Iauaretê após 22 anos e iniciam projeto de atendimento a indígenas no AM — Foto: Divulgação

Os Expedicionários da Saúde (EDS) iniciaram no sábado (31) uma nova expedição médica em Iauaretê, em São Gabriel da Cachoeira , no Alto Rio Negro, no interior do Amazonas. A ação marca o início do projeto "Cuidar para Preservar", que prevê quatro anos de atendimento a comunidades indígenas da região. O local foi escolhido por ter recebido a primeira expedição da organização, em abril de 2004.

Os atendimentos seguem até 7 de novembro. Cerca de 60 profissionais e voluntários, entre médicos, enfermeiros e equipes de apoio, participam da ação.

A 59ª expedição oferece serviços em quatro áreas: oftalmologia, cirurgia geral, saúde da mulher e pediatria.

Na oftalmologia, estão previstas cirurgias de catarata e pterígio. Já na cirurgia geral, a equipe dará atenção especial a pacientes com hérnia. Na saúde da mulher, o trabalho inclui prevenção e diagnóstico precoce do câncer do colo do útero.

Também serão realizados exames, avaliações e ações de prevenção e acompanhamento de pacientes, conforme as necessidades das comunidades.

Projeto prevê quatro anos de atendimento

O projeto "Cuidar para Preservar" tem duração prevista de quatro anos e conta com apoio do Fundo Amazônia, gerido pelo Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social ( BNDES ).

Além das expedições médicas e cirúrgicas, a iniciativa prevê atendimento odontológico, consultas a distância, capacitação de profissionais locais e melhorias na estrutura dos polos de saúde indígena.

O projeto também inclui atendimento a pessoas amputadas, com fornecimento de próteses por meio do programa Floresta em Movimento.

A proposta é ampliar o acesso a serviços especializados e fortalecer o atendimento de saúde nas comunidades indígenas do Alto Rio Negro.

Estrutura leva centro cirúrgico à região

Para realizar os atendimentos, a organização mobiliza uma estrutura hospitalar móvel, com centro cirúrgico e equipamentos usados em hospitais de grandes cidades.

A operação envolve cerca de 20 toneladas de equipamentos, medicamentos e materiais. O transporte até Iauaretê exige trechos por rios e deslocamentos terrestres, devido à dificuldade de acesso à região.

Na primeira expedição, em 2004, a equipe era formada por quatro médicos e transportava cerca de 100 quilos de materiais. Atualmente, a organização mobiliza dezenas de profissionais e uma estrutura capaz de realizar cirurgias em áreas remotas.

Em mais de 20 anos de atuação, os Expedicionários da Saúde realizaram 58 expedições, mais de 11 mil cirurgias, 80 mil atendimentos e 170 mil exames.

O projeto é desenvolvido em parceria com instituições de saúde e organizações indígenas que atuam na região, entre elas o Distrito Sanitário Especial Indígena do Alto Rio Negro (DSEI-ARN) e a Federação das Organizações Indígenas do Rio Negro (FOIRN).

articles.title: Por que Trump enfrenta o mesmo problema econômico que derrubou Biden | G1
articles.standfirst: Donald Trump chega às eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos com um problema semelhante ao enfrentado pelo ex-presidente democrata.
articles.summary: Donald Trump chega às eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos com um problema semelhante ao enfrentado pelo ex-presidente democrata.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e seu antecessor, Joe Biden. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A Casa Branca enfrenta um dilema conhecido.

Os indicadores econômicos não são necessariamente ruins, mas a opinião pública nos Estados Unidos é negativa.

Essa desconexão perseguiu Joe Biden em 2024, quando os principais indicadores, embora sólidos, não conseguiram convencer muitos eleitores de que a economia estava funcionando a seu favor.

Agora, Donald Trump enfrenta uma versão diferente do mesmo desafio.

Durante a campanha de 2024, Trump prometeu aos eleitores um alívio rápido para a inflação.

"Quando eu vencer, vou baixar os preços imediatamente", disse.

Cumprir essa promessa tem sido mais difícil do que o esperado.

O crescimento econômico permanece estável, o desemprego continua baixo e o mercado de ações está perto de suas máximas históricas.

Mas o relatório mais recente sobre a inflação antes das eleições de meio de mandato confirma o que os eleitores já sabem: os preços continuam altos.

Biden lidava com as consequências da pandemia de covid.

Trump enfrenta preços mais altos da energia , relacionados ao conflito entre Estados Unidos e Israel contra o Irã , além dos efeitos de algumas de suas próprias políticas comerciais e migratórias.

A realidade política, no entanto, é muito semelhante.

Os eleitores não avaliam a economia pelos números do PIB ou pelas máximas históricas do mercado de ações.

Eles a avaliam pelo que pagam no supermercado, pelo preço da gasolina e pela capacidade de arcar com suas despesas.

Os números contam apenas parte da história

Um crescimento econômico de 2,2% nos Estados Unidos seria respeitável pelos padrões de muitas economias ricas.

A Alemanha, por exemplo, tem enfrentado dificuldades para alcançar um dinamismo semelhante. E uma taxa de desemprego estável de 4,2% nos EUA dificilmente indica uma economia em queda livre.

Trump argumenta que herdou de Biden um desastre econômico e aponta o forte crescimento, os investimentos e o bom desempenho do mercado de ações como provas de que suas políticas estão funcionando.

Após a divulgação do relatório mais recente sobre a inflação, o porta-voz da Casa Branca, Matthew Middleton, afirmou que a "agenda econômica favorável ao crescimento" do governo havia amenizado "a crise inflacionária de Biden".

Larry Kudlow, aliado de Trump e comentarista econômico, descreveu a atual expansão como "a melhor história já contada" e afirmou que "ninguém será demitido".

Os eleitores parecem estar interpretando uma história diferente: Trump venceu a eleição presidencial prometendo enfrentar o alto custo de vida, mas os preços continuam subindo.

Parte do problema é que os aumentos salariais não acompanharam o ritmo da alta dos preços.

O salário médio por hora subiu 3% no último ano, enquanto os preços ao consumidor aumentaram 3,7%.

Isso ajuda a explicar por que as pesquisas continuam mostrando que os eleitores avaliam negativamente a atuação de Trump na economia.

Para os democratas, essa dinâmica é familiar.

Celinda Lake, uma experiente pesquisadora de opinião pública ligada ao Partido Democrata, afirma que o problema começa na maneira como economistas e eleitores usam as mesmas palavras para falar de coisas diferentes.

"Quando os economistas dizem que a inflação está caindo, querem dizer que o ritmo de aumento dos preços diminuiu", afirma.

Biden baseou sua campanha de 2024 na economia, mas os eleitores tinham uma percepção diferente. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

"Quando os eleitores dizem que a inflação caiu, querem dizer que os preços voltaram ao patamar anterior. Bem, é claro que isso nunca acontece", explica.

O governo Biden passou boa parte de 2024 destacando o baixo desemprego, o crescimento sólido e a queda da inflação.

Ainda assim, muitos eleitores continuavam pensando nos preços elevados que enfrentavam diariamente.

Lake, que assessorou a campanha de Biden em 2020, mas não participou da disputa de 2024, afirma que os eleitores avaliam a economia com base em suas experiências pessoais, e não nos indicadores econômicos.

"Não é possível discutir com as pessoas sobre a realidade da vida delas", afirma.

Isso pode ajudar a explicar por que o desafio de Trump se parece tanto com o de Biden.

Os críticos de Biden o responsabilizaram pela inflação. Mas ele poderia apontar fatores que estavam, em grande parte, fora de seu controle, como a pandemia e seus efeitos sobre as cadeias de abastecimento.

Alguns economistas afirmam que os preços mais altos de hoje são, pelo menos em parte, resultado de suas próprias políticas, incluindo as tarifas comerciais, além das consequências econômicas da guerra entre Estados Unidos e Israel contra o Irã.

"A inflação é claramente atribuível a Donald Trump ", avalia Peter Morici, economista da Universidade de Maryland alinhado aos republicanos.

"São as tarifas dele e a guerra. As pessoas sabem disso. Elas veem", acrescenta.

As tarifas do chamado "Dia da Libertação" de Trump, anunciadas em abril de 2025, elevaram os custos para os consumidores.

Um estudo do Federal Reserve de Nova York concluiu que as tarifas aumentaram os preços dos bens de consumo em aproximadamente 2,9%.

Presidente americano, Donald Trump. — Foto: Reuters via BBC

O impacto poderia ter sido maior se Trump não tivesse suspendido posteriormente algumas tarifas, fechado novos acordos comerciais e se a Suprema Corte não o tivesse impedido de usar poderes de emergência para impor muitas outras taxas sobre importações.

O conflito com o Irã elevou os preços do petróleo, encarecendo a gasolina e pressionando ainda mais o orçamento das famílias.

A Casa Branca aponta os cortes de impostos, o crescimento do emprego e a redução do custo dos medicamentos vendidos sob prescrição como provas de que está cumprindo seus compromissos com as famílias americanas.

Além disso, o governo vem adotando cada vez mais políticas destinadas a aliviar as pressões econômicas.

Trump pediu que seja estabelecido um limite para as taxas de juros dos cartões de crédito e levantou a possibilidade de um pagamento de US$ 5 mil aos adultos americanos caso os republicanos mantenham o controle do Congresso.

Essas medidas refletem uma realidade política familiar aos dois partidos: quando os eleitores estão preocupados com os preços, argumentos sobre crescimento sólido e baixo desemprego raramente são suficientes.

Biden nunca encontrou uma maneira de diminuir a distância entre o desempenho da economia e a confiança dos eleitores nela.

A pergunta às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato é se Trump conseguirá fazer isso.

Se a história política recente servir de referência, a percepção sobre a economia pode importar mais do que os próprios indicadores econômicos.

articles.title: Petrobras aumenta preço do querosene de aviação em novembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Aumento será de 7,2%, o que corresponde a R$ 0,45 por litro em relação ao mês anterior.
articles.summary: Aumento será de 7,2%, o que corresponde a R$ 0,45 por litro em relação ao mês anterior.
articles.body:
A Petrobras anunciou um novo aumento no preço de venda do querosene de aviação (QAV) para as distribuidoras a partir deste domingo (1º). O reajuste será de 7,2%, o equivalente a R$ 0,45 por litro em relação ao mês anterior.

Este é mais um aumento consecutivo do combustível. Em outubro, o preço subiu cerca de 12% em algumas das principais bases de distribuição do país, depois de uma alta média de aproximadamente 13,9% em setembro.

Segundo a companhia, o reajuste reflete a alta das cotações internacionais do QAV, em meio às tensões geopolíticas no Oriente Médio e à redução da capacidade de refino na Rússia e na Ucrânia em decorrência da guerra entre os dois países.

Os preços do QAV vendido pela Petrobras às distribuidoras são ajustados no início de cada mês, conforme previsto nos contratos.

Segundo a estatal, a fórmula usada para definir o preço do combustível no mercado brasileiro reduz as oscilações no curto prazo, o que resulta em reajustes mais moderados do que os observados no exterior.

"Nos principais mercados internacionais, os preços do QAV destinados às companhias aéreas são ajustados com maior frequência, podendo chegar a revisões diárias, o que faz com que reflitam mais rapidamente as condições de mercado", explicou a companhia em nota.

"Nesse contexto, as variações acumuladas desde o início do conflito têm sido superiores nos mercados internacionais às observadas no Brasil, indicando que o preço do QAV da Petrobras permanece competitivo", acrescentou.

articles.title: Sandisk (SNDK) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Cut As Analysts Weigh AI Demand
articles.summary: Sandisk’s modeled fair value has shifted from US$2,173.00 to US$2,105.29, pointing to a modestly lower price target in the latest update. This change lines u...
articles.body:
Sandisk's modeled fair value has shifted from US$2,173.00 to US$2,105.29, pointing to a modestly lower price target in the latest update. This change lines up with a mixed analyst backdrop, where enthusiasm around AI driven NAND demand and new business terms is tempered by concerns about sector multiple compression and how resilient today's conditions will be. As you read on, you will see how these moving pieces shape the evolving Sandisk story and what to watch next.

Stay updated as the Fair Value for Sandisk shifts by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio . Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on Sandisk.

Several firms, including Evercore ISI, Mizuho, Rosenblatt, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, highlight Sandisk as a key beneficiary of AI driven NAND demand, with Outperform or Buy ratings anchored in long term data center and enterprise storage growth themes.

Rosenblatt and Evercore point to Sandisk's technology roadmap and partnership with Kioxia as support for competitive bit cost and performance in AI oriented storage, while Evercore also emphasizes multi year demand visibility and high bandwidth flash opportunities.

JPMorgan and Wells Fargo reference the new business model framework and non bit manufacturing economics, which they see as supportive of structurally higher margins and reduced cyclicality, although they still view the valuation reset as a gradual process.

Argus cites strong reported Q4 results and momentum in data center and solid state drive solutions, and Morgan Stanley views the plan to return 100% of cash flow alongside moderate investment as a clear positive for capital allocation discipline.

RBC Capital, Citi, Jefferies and Mizuho have all trimmed Sandisk price targets over recent months, often pointing to sector multiple compression, more muted NAND pricing and questions around the durability of peak margin conditions.

Jefferies flags investor focus on moderating pricing, lower gross margin guidance and possible near term headwinds from Edge inventory builds, while Morgan Stanley is not fully convinced that industry improvements are more structural than cyclical.

Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. Head to the Simply Wall St Community to discover more perspectives!

How This Changes the Fair Value For Sandisk

The modeled fair value for Sandisk has shifted from US$2,173.00 to US$2,105.29.

The revenue growth assumption has moved from 40.74% to 27.18%.

The net profit margin assumption has changed from 65.19% to 50.47%.

The future P/E assumption has adjusted from 11.02x to 12.21x.

The discount rate has been updated from 8.53% to 8.48%.

articles.title: India's record oil imports hit 5.6 million bpd as Middle East, Russia supplies rise: Report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's crude oil imports hit a record high of around 5.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, with refiners stepping up purchases from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's crude oil imports hit a record high of around 5.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, with refiners stepping up purchases from both the Middle East and Russia. While improved supplies through the Strait of Hormuz have boosted Gulf shipments, rising freight costs could make Russian crude less attractive in the coming months, according to energy intelligence firm Kpler.Middle Eastern supplies accounted for about 2.3 million bpd, while Russian shipments remained strong at nearly 2 million bpd, Kpler lead analyst Nikhil Dubey said, as quoted by PTI.The increase in Gulf supplies comes as more crude is moving through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil trade. Higher ship-to-ship transfers helped boost flows through the strait during September and October.Gulf producers are also offering competitive delivered prices to regain market share in India. This could make their supplies more attractive to refiners in the coming months, particularly as the cost of transporting Russian crude rises.Dubey said Russian shipments could moderate in November and December as attacks in the Black Sea push up freight rates, reducing the price advantage of Russian oil once transportation costs are included."Russian flows, which have held strong at these levels, could soften in November-December as attacks in the Black Sea push freight rates higher, making Russian barrels less attractive on a landed cost basis," he said.However, a shift towards Middle Eastern supplies may depend on how the situation around Hormuz unfolds. Any renewed disruption to shipments through the strait could make Gulf crude harder to secure and prompt Indian refiners to return to Russian barrels, even at higher freight costs."The situation remains volatile, and any renewed disruption to Hormuz flows could see refiners turning back to Russian barrels, even at higher freight costs," Dubey said.The October 16 waiver under the Graham Act could also ease concerns among some Indian buyers about the risks associated with purchasing Russian oil, giving them greater flexibility in sourcing supplies, he added.India imports nearly 90 per cent of its crude oil requirements, making the availability, transportation costs and final landed price of different grades important factors in procurement decisions.How Russia became a key supplierIndia's dependence on Russian crude rose sharply after Moscow invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Western sanctions, the European Union's ban on seaborne Russian crude and a G7 price cap disrupted Russia's traditional oil trade, forcing it to look for alternative buyers.With European refiners turning away from Russian supplies, Moscow offered steep discounts to attract customers. Indian refiners emerged as major buyers, with Russian crude eventually accounting for as much as 40-50 per cent of India's oil basket at its peak.The price advantage was significant. Russian Urals crude traded at discounts of around $30 per barrel to Brent at times in late 2022 and early 2023, making it an attractive option for Indian refiners seeking to lower input costs.Those discounts have since narrowed. Yet Russian shipments have remained substantial, partly because disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies have made alternative sources important for India's energy security.You use AI every day. articles.title: GST collections rise 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, supported by a sharp
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, supported by a sharp increase in revenue from imports and steady growth in domestic collections, provisional government data showed on Sunday.The October collection compares with Rs 1.88 lakh crore recorded in the same month last year. After adjusting for refunds, net GST revenue grew 25.6 per cent to Rs 2.03 lakh crore, against Rs 1.61 lakh crore a year ago.Revenue from imports was the bigger contributor to the increase, rising 42.2 per cent to Rs 72,246 crore from Rs 50,796 crore in October 2025. Collections from domestic transactions grew 15.8 per cent to Rs 1.59 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.37 lakh crore in the year-ago period.The government issued refunds worth Rs 27,934 crore during the month, 6.5 per cent higher than in October last year. Domestic refunds increased 9.8 per cent to Rs 14,007 crore, while refunds on imports rose 3.4 per cent to Rs 13,927 crore.After adjusting for refunds, net revenue from domestic transactions grew 16.4 per cent to Rs 1.45 lakh crore. Net collections from customs-related GST rose 56.2 per cent to Rs 58,319 crore.Among major states, Maharashtra recorded domestic GST collections of Rs 35,150 crore, up 13 per cent year-on-year. Karnataka's collections increased 18 per cent to Rs 15,922 crore, while Gujarat reported a 16 per cent rise to Rs 13,516 crore. Haryana recorded a 17 per cent increase to Rs 11,529 crore.Assam saw one of the sharpest increases, with collections rising 47 per cent to Rs 1,934 crore. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar both recorded 24 per cent growth."October’s gross GST collections of Rs 2.31 lakh crore, registering a robust 22.9% year-on-year growth, reinforce the continued buoyancy in GST revenues. Importantly, this strength is not limited to a single month, with cumulative gross collections during April–October reaching Rs 14.78 lakh crore, representing a healthy 13.2% year-on-year growth. This sustained revenue buoyancy, despite bold rate cuts mid last year, is providing the confidence and headroom for the GST Council to continue with the reform express," said Mahesh Jaising, partner & leader indirect tax, Deloitte India.While, Abhishek Jain, partner and national head indirect tax for Kpmg in India, said, “The GST collection figures with a growth of 22.9% for October 2026 is impressive and adds to the festive cheer. The cumulative gross GST collections for April–October 2026 have also grown by 13.2% reflecting sustained economic activity, improved tax compliance and the continued resilience of India's consumption and trade ecosystem. Overall, the October numbers provide a positive signal for revenue mobilisation and reinforce the growing maturity of India's GST framework.”Nitin Vijaivergia, partner, Price Waterhouse & Co LLP, also higlhighted the strong momentum saying, "October’s GST collections of Rs 2.31 lakh crore, the second-highest monthly collection on record, reflect strong revenue momentum. Domestic collections grew 15.8%, signalling healthy consumption and economic activity, while import revenues surged 42.2%, highlighting the increasing contribution of imports to overall GST revenues. This trend merits attention from a domestic manufacturing perspective. Encouragingly, net GST revenues grew even faster at 25.6%, with refunds rising only 6.5%. Cumulative April-October collections grew 13.2%, further indicating that the revenue buoyancy is broad-based and extends beyond a single month."For the first seven months of the current financial year, gross GST collections rose 13.2 per cent to Rs 14.77 lakh crore, compared with Rs 13.05 lakh crore during April-October last year. Net collections during the period increased 12.6 per cent to Rs 12.69 lakh crore.The October figures mark a strong year-on-year increase in tax collections, with both domestic activity and imports contributing to the growth.You use AI every day. articles.title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 34,843 crore from Indian stocks; second straight month of selling spree
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) withdrew Rs 34,843 crore from Indian equities in October, marking the second consecutive month of substantial outflows
articles.body: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) withdrew Rs 34,843 crore from Indian equities in October, marking the second consecutive month of substantial outflows amid concerns over high crude oil prices, global interest rates and the outlook for corporate earnings.However, foreign investors turned net buyers towards the end of the month, purchasing equities worth around Rs 6,300 crore between October 26 and 30.This followed net withdrawals of nearly Rs 2,700 crore in the week ended October 23, according to data from the Central Depository Services Ltd (CDSL).The latest buying indicates an improvement in near-term investor sentiment, although market experts cautioned that a single week of positive flows does not necessarily signal a sustained reversal.FPI outflows from Indian equities reach Rs 2.95 lakh crore in 2026Foreign investors had withdrawn Rs 35,861 crore from Indian equities in September. Before that, they invested Rs 20,200 crore in July and Rs 29,631 crore in August.With October's withdrawals, cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities in 2026 have reached Rs 2.95 lakh crore.Anand K Rathi, co-founder of MIRA Money, said foreign selling remained significant through October, reflecting concerns over elevated crude prices, global interest rates and corporate earnings prospects.“Higher crude prices pose risks to India's inflation and corporate margins, and attractive yields in the US continue to influence global capital allocation,” he said.Rathi added that the sustainability of the recent improvement in foreign flows would depend on greater clarity over global macroeconomic conditions, crude prices and the earnings outlook. He also pointed to the role of domestic institutional investors in absorbing foreign selling and supporting market stability.Fed decision, valuations among factors behind late-month buyingFPIs were net buyers in three of the four trading sessions ending October 30 in the cash market, suggesting a possible improvement in their outlook towards Indian equities.VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said the US Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged, attractive valuations in Indian large-cap stocks and signs of sustained domestic economic growth could have contributed to the shift in sentiment.The weakening of the global artificial intelligence trade could also be influencing portfolio allocations, he added.The improvement in foreign investment flows helped the Nifty reclaim the 23,000 mark.Vijayakumar said that while foreign investors continued to sell large-cap financial stocks, they were selectively accumulating pharmaceutical and healthcare shares, along with stocks of certain digital platform companies.Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice-president for research at Bajaj Broking, said the reversal in FPI flows was encouraging for market sentiment. However, elevated crude prices and global event-related risks could restrict the momentum.Market participants will closely watch the outcome of the US midterm elections in the coming week, along with movements in Brent crude prices, developments in the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, and quarterly corporate earnings announcements.These factors are expected to remain important drivers of foreign investment flows and broader market sentiment in the near term.You use AI every day. articles.title: IGL to supply PNG to 22 northern railway facilities
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Public sector Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) has signed an agreement with the Delhi division of Northern Railway for the supply of PNG to 22
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Public sector Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) has signed an agreement with the Delhi division of Northern Railway for the supply of PNG to 22 railway establishments in Delhi-NCR, as part of its efforts to replace diesel and LPG with natural gas.IGL said piped natural gas will be used for boiler operations at mechanised laundries at Delhi Sarai Rohilla, Old Delhi, Anand Vihar Terminal, Hazrat Nizamuddin and New Delhi railway stations, besides officers’ rest houses, base kitchens, running rooms, subordinate rest houses, and guard and TTE lobbies in Delhi, Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar.The initiative is part of govt’s efforts to expand the use of piped gas under PNG Drive 3.0, which was launched on Oct 1 to increase domestic and commercial PNG connections.IGL said initial PNG consumption under the agreement is estimated at nearly 3,000 standard cubic metres per day (SCMD), replacing daily consumption of about 500 kg of LPG and 2,500 litres of diesel.“By facilitating the transition from LPG and diesel to PNG, the partnership is expected to simplify fuel handling, strengthen supply reliability and reduce dependence on conventional liquid fuels,” IGL said in a statement, adding that the initiative will help expand the natural gas ecosystem and support India’s transition towards a “cleaner, convenient, cost effective, continuous, secure, and sustainable energy future”.IGL chairman Subhankar Sen said the agreement will facilitate the replacement of a substantial quantity of LPG with natural gas, thereby helping reduce import dependence and the subsidy burden.Pushpesh Raman Tripathi, DRM, Delhi Division, Northern Railway, said plans were afoot to extend PNG connectivity to railway hospitals and residential colonies in the future.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Coming into this week, all eyes will be on potential sparks to re-light the fire under the tech sector. Fire, to be clear, in a bad way.
articles.body:
Last week, we opened the Morning Brief newsletter by saying the first week of Big Tech earnings looked promising — until Thursday. This time, we're here to say the second week of Big Tech earnings looked promising — until Tuesday.

Lackluster earnings from Alphabet ( GOOG ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Intel ( INTC ) sent the tech complex into a steep sell-off, ending a wild week that began with Anthropic's S-1 filing.

Coming into this week, all eyes will be on potential sparks to relight the fire under the tech sector. Fire, to be clear, in a bad way.

Kicking off the week on Monday are earnings from Apple ( AAPL ) and Palantir ( PLTR ), alongside Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ) and Lattice Semiconductor ( LSCC ) in the chips sector.

On Tuesday, our focus shifts to politics, as US midterms are set to influence everything from control of Congress and the Iran war to the data center boom. On top of that, AMD ( AMD ) and Marathon Petroleum Corporation ( MPC ) both report earnings, and the US government will report JOLTS data in the first major labor market update of the week.

Wednesday and Thursday bring earnings from Toyota Motor ( TM ), ConocoPhillips ( COP ), Eaton Corporation ( ETN ), Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), and a range of other corporate market heavyweights, alongside a smattering of economic data.

And all of that excitement sets up Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report, the banner data release of the week.

Big Tech's sell-off wasn't about the actual fundamentals

It was a deeply red week for the tech sector after a slew of earnings failed to give investors the signs of strength they were looking (and hoping) for.

At Alphabet, a miss on both revenue and profit sent shares falling 13% as Sundar Pichai said that while the company's search division had grown, the money wasn't keeping up as AI cuts into search monetization.

Down the street at Amazon, a double miss on both earnings and revenue triggered a sell-off that couldn't be stopped by strong cloud growth in AWS.

And we can't forget Intel, where a beat on earnings and in-line revenue were overshadowed by weakness in PC sales, attributed to heightened memory costs. That company lost a quarter of its value after the report, falling over 28%.

But there's a conundrum for investors in these earnings reports. As Barron's associate editor Al Root said to Yahoo Finance, the numbers weren't all bad; it's more like investors have gotten more demanding.

"It's not that the earnings were awful, it's just that it wasn't enough to support the market," Root said on "The 8:30." He added, "The level of nerves going into earnings season was so high, like everybody was waiting for the shoe to drop."

It's a mistake that could be jeopardizing your finances: Nearly nine out of 10 people (86%) said "they've stalled on a debt decision (1)" when surveyed by fintech platform Rose Cove. Why? More than one-third (36%) of respondents cite "too many options" as a reason for doing so.

articles.title: Trump says wives are falling back in love with their husbands after seeing their surging 401(k) balances
articles.summary: While Trump is taking credit for both rising retirement balances and happier marriages, just how much have Americans’ 401(k)s actually grown?
articles.body:
Money may not be able to buy love, but President Donald Trump seems to think a soaring 401(k) balance can help bring it back.

During an October 29 campaign rally in Rock Hill, South Carolina, Trump claimed that the stock market's gains under his administration have done more than boost Americans' retirement savings. According to the president, they've even helped rekindle the romance in some marriages.

The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 moves to make before the window closes

"I've had wives tell me that they love their husband again...'My husband is a great investor. He's up 67%.' That's me that did it!" Trump told the crowd .

But while Trump is taking credit for both rising retirement balances and happier marriages, just how much have Americans' 401(k)s actually grown?

Trump's comments weren't just about retirement savings. They were also part of a pitch to voters ahead of the November midterm elections . The president encouraged Americans to check their 401(k) balances before heading to the polls, claiming the stock market had reached 88 all-time highs since his election and that retirement accounts were doing better than ever.

There's certainly some good news for Americans saving for retirement. According to Fidelity Investments' latest retirement analysis , the average 401(k) balance reached a record $155,800 in the second quarter of 2026, up 13% from the same period last year. Looking back a decade, balances have jumped 75%.

The stock market has also been having a pretty good year. As of October 29, the S&P 500 was up 12.8% since the beginning of 2026, according to The Associated Press .

But before Americans start celebrating their newfound wealth, there's a little more to the story. A growing 401(k) balance doesn't necessarily mean investments alone are delivering those returns. Retirement accounts also grow through contributions from employees and their employers.

And averages can be misleading. According to Vanguard's 2026 How America Saves report , the median retirement plan balance among its participants was just $44,115 at the end of 2025. That means half had less than that amount in their accounts. People with very large retirement accounts can pull the average up, making it seem like the typical saver has more tucked away than they actually do.

articles.title: Wall Street Braces for More Wild Days in Stocks After Tech Rout
articles.summary: The stock market got a long-awaited jolt of volatility late last week after disappointing earnings from technology giants added to angst around the AI-driven...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The stock market got a long-awaited jolt of volatility late last week after disappointing earnings from technology giants added to angst around the AI-driven rally.

Now traders are bracing for further shocks this week from the US midterm elections and Nvidia Corp. earnings later in November.

The Cboe Volatility Index on Friday touched the highest intraday level since April as the S&P 500 dropped the most since June. The premium for puts protecting against further losses also surged, as did correlations among stocks, which can signal broader stress in the market. Still, those measures remain well below the levels in March after the US and Israel attacked Iran.

With Nvidia due to report earnings, following disappointing results from Amazon.com Inc., Alphabet Inc. and Intel Corp., investors are preparing for more episodes of volatility. Traders are also eyeing US midterm election results for the potential effect on the war in Iran and domestic economic policy.

"This looks more like a bullish rotation with a derating at its core than the beginning of a broad market deterioration.," said Florian Ielpo, head of macro research at Lombard Odier Investment Management.

So far, the latest selloff has been largely focused on the technology sector, with investors rotating away from the high-flying firms that led the gains this year. Realized 60-day volatility on the US benchmark last week touched the lowest in more than a year, with the low correlation this year and tendency of zero-day options traders to buy dips and sell rallies helping to restrain moves.

The late-week slide comes in a year that's been relatively placid. While 2025 saw a cluster of extreme market swings around the tariff tumult in April, in 2026 US stocks have largely shrugged off spikes in oil prices and interest rates.

But even as the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 capped its worst month since 2025, some investors were betting on a recovery. There were pockets of call and call spread buying seen Friday on the benchmark indexes and some of the most beaten-down tech names such as Intel.

Options were relatively pricey before the larger gyrations late in the week, with the VIX at the higher end of the range over the past five years compared with 20-day realized swings.

articles.title: AI may automate routine IT work. These are the skills that could command a pay premium
articles.summary: By Neeti Sharma, CEO, TeamLease Digital The contemporary enterprise operates in an environment defined by unprecedented geopolitical volatility, economic
articles.body: By Neeti Sharma, CEO, TeamLease DigitalThe contemporary enterprise operates in an environment defined by unprecedented geopolitical volatility, economic shifts, and rapid technological acceleration. Across the Asia-Pacific region, 81% of senior leaders identify the capacity to operate effectively amid constant change and uncertainty as an indispensable leadership requirement. Against this backdrop, artificial intelligence is shifting from a technological initiative to the core operating model.India’s tech ecosystem is undergoing a structural transition: the shift from AI Fluency to AI Capability.The Literacy Stage: Individual experimentation, tool usage, and basic prompt engineering.The Fluency Stage: Integration of AI into role-specific workflows and task-level automation.The Capability Stage: Enterprise-grade production where AI systems are deployed, secured, governed, and scaled with named human accountability.While 81% of APAC midmarket enterprises have embedded AI into daily operations, only 27% report that their leaders are fully prepared to integrate AI-generated insights, exercise critical judgment, and manage compound risk. As execution costs collapse toward zero, compensation and enterprise value are decoupling from traditional job titles and tenure. Instead, value is concentrating at the intersection of technical depth, domain context, and human judgment.The Re-Pricing of Digital TalentAn analysis of over 37,000 technology and digital roles shows that traditional valuation proxies—such as headcount, geographic tier, and years of service- no longer accurately predict market value.Consider a stark market anomaly: a GenAI engineer in Indore commands a median fixed salary of Rs 16.5 LPA, out-earning a cybersecurity engineer in Bengaluru at Rs 14.4 LPA. Skill tier and capability proximity now supersede location and legacy tenure.Enterprise Talent Tiering ModelAI-Core Tier: Roles that build, own, and govern intelligent systems open at Rs 13.2 LPA for early-career roles, with projected annual growth of 16% to 21%. Compensation scales at 2.5x to 3.0x baseline levels.AI-Adjacent Tier: Roles that apply AI in core workflows command mid-tier premiums.AI-Support Tier: Roles focused on routine monitoring, data QA, and first-line maintenance open between Rs 4.8 and 5.4 LPA, growing at a modest 7% to 8%.The resulting 2.5x to 3.0x entry pay differential compounds over time. This divergence represents a structural scarcity premium. Only 16% of India’s technology workforce currently possesses advanced AI capabilities, against an enterprise talent deficit of 53% to 60% in GenAI and cloud architectures.Prompting and basic tool usage have quickly become table stakes. The durable premium accrues to professionals who can bridge technical execution with risk oversight, domain nuance, and business accountability.The Verification Bottleneck and Executive OversightAs AI models handle increasingly sophisticated analytical and generative tasks, organizations face a subtle operational risk: equating polished analysis with sound judgment.Generative tools can produce well-formatted code, market assessments, or legal summaries that look authoritative while masking flawed assumptions or outdated regulatory inputs. While AI expands the volume of intelligence, it cannot verify its own contextual accuracy.This dynamic creates an operational bottleneck. Enterprise survey data indicates that 66% of organizations struggle with stakeholder trust issues related to AI output, data privacy, and ethical compliance. Furthermore, only 15% of APAC CEOs report achieving both revenue expansion and cost reduction from their AI investments, with half seeing neither benefit yet.The bottleneck is rarely the technology itself; it is the organizational capacity to evaluate, govern, and operationalize model outputs. Senior leadership must shift focus from acquiring pure execution capacity to developing Architects of Inquiry, leaders who use domain expertise not to supply canned answers, but to ask the critical questions that surface hidden assumptions, missing evidence, and edge-case risks.The Enterprise Governance Blueprint for Human-in-the-Loop OperationsTo successfully balance AI adoption with operational integrity, organizations require a repeatable operational framework. "Human-in-the-loop" cannot remain a vague supervisory concept; it must be operationalized across four key pillars:Strategic Framing: Before deploying models, human leads must define the business problem, operational boundaries, regulatory constraints, and acceptable error tolerances. Without explicit framing, AI systems risk optimizing for the wrong objectives.Rigorous Challenge: Outputs must be subjected to systemic stress-testing. Leaders must cultivate a culture that asks: What assumptions underly this result? What data was omitted? Where does this model fail in edge cases?Named Accountability: Every automated workflow reaching production must have a named human owner who accepts legal, financial, and operational responsibility for its outcomes.A Cloud Security Architect lets AI automate threat triage, but retains ownership over breach containment decisions.A Data Architect uses automated pipelines, but owns the ultimate integrity and regulatory compliance of the data estate.Deterministic Escalation: Organizations must institute explicit protocols defining when an AI system must yield to human judgment. Workflows containing high legal, reputational, or financial risk require mandatory human sign-off.This framework applies equally across functional areas. In finance, marketing, HR, and supply chain operations, AI handles preliminary synthesis, shifting human effort toward trade-off evaluation, strategic alignment, and stakeholder trust.Senior compensation ceilings illustrate this shift. At 15+ years of experience, compensation is set by enterprise trust, governance, and architecture scale rather than raw code volume:AI Architect: Rs 108.6 LPAIndustrial Data Architect: Rs 102.6 LPAOT Security Architect: Rs 95.8 LPAWorkforce Vulnerability and the Early-Career Capability PipelineThe transition toward AI-driven execution exposes a sharp divide in the talent market. Routine execution roles, such as repetitive reporting, manual software testing, first-line support, and rule-based data processing, are undergoing structural compression. Across GCCs and enterprise technology providers, zero AI-Support roles feature among high-growth premium categories.Task automation presents a systemic challenge for talent development: the erosion of the entry-level learning pipeline. Historically, professionals developed judgment by working through routine, task-level problems. If AI platforms absorb these baseline responsibilities, enterprises risk interrupting the natural development pipeline required to cultivate future architects and decision-makers.Organizations must re-architect entry-level roles. Instead of assigning junior staff to manual execution, companies should integrate early-career talent directly into human-AI "fusion roles". In these roles, junior staff learn by reviewing AI-generated outputs, evaluating edge cases alongside senior mentors, and participating directly in verification workflows.Executive Strategies for Workforce AdaptationTo navigate the shift from AI adoption to govern enterprise capability, leadership should prioritize three strategic imperatives:1. Transition from Experimental Pilots to Governed ProductionProof-of-concept projects rarely generate durable enterprise value or capability depth. Organizational resources must focus on embedding AI inside live operational workflows backed by explicit governance mechanisms. Capability development should move talent systematically through structured pathways: from experimental sandboxes to manager-nominated production deployments and formal model evaluation roles.2. Drive Lateral Capability Reskilling Across Adjacent TracksBecause off-the-shelf senior talent is scarce, enterprise agility depends on internal mobility and reskilling. The most cost-effective path to building capacity is moving experienced domain professionals into adjacent, high-demand technical tracks:Test Automation Engineers transitioning into Quality & Platform OperationsBusiness Analysts evolving into Decision Intelligence & Data Product ManagementInfrastructure Engineers pivoting to Cloud Security & GRC GovernanceMoving professionals into higher-value capability tracks yields significant productivity returns compared to static internal progression. Combining deep domain knowledge with AI capability creates talent that is difficult to replace.3. Institutionalize Critical Inquiry as an Enterprise DisciplineOrganizations should establish formal operational routines that reward critical thinking and structured skepticism. Enterprise initiatives should include:Scenario & Stress-Testing Drills: Pairing technical engineers with domain leads to stress-test model outputs under simulated failure conditions.Portfolio & Verification Standards: Evaluating talent based on tangible deployment outcomes, architectural contributions, and documented governance decisions rather than abstract tool certifications.Technology cycles will continue to accelerate, rendering specific toolsets obsolete. What remains durable is the enterprise capacity to govern complex systems, make reasoned trade-offs under uncertainty, and maintain institutional trust.Enterprise readiness is ultimately measured not by total headcount or the sheer volume of AI deployment, but by capability depth and decision quality. In an AI-augmented economy, competitive advantage belongs to the organizations and leaders, those who balance fast technological execution with rigorous, accountable judgment.(The author is CEO, TeamLease Digital)You use AI every day.
