articles.title: Billionaire tax divides California Democrats, draws myriad questions
articles.summary: California voters this midterm cycle will decide whether the state will impose a wealth tax on billionaire residents, as wealthy Californians organize against the measure and experts say its potential broader impact on the state’s economy is nuanced. By voting “yes” on Proposition 40, Californians would support a one-time 5 percent tax on billionaires’ wealth.…
articles.body:
California voters this midterm cycle will decide whether the state will impose a wealth tax on billionaire residents, as wealthy Californians organize against the measure and experts say its potential broader impact on the state’s economy is nuanced.

By voting “yes” on Proposition 40 , Californians would support a one-time 5 percent tax on billionaires’ wealth. The government revenue from the wealth tax — which no state to date has imposed — would primarily go toward state healthcare programs, with the remainder earmarked for food assistance and education initiatives.

The Golden State would collect “tens of billions of dollars” from the wealth tax on the roughly 200 billionaires in the state, per an analysis from the nonpartisan state Legislative Analyst’s Office (LAO), which noted the increase in revenue would be “ spread across several years .”

But polling indicates it is unclear the measure will receive the simple majority support needed to pass. Even if it does, questions remain about next steps for the state and downstream effects.

“When you see eye-popping numbers like that, I can see how that looks … very appealing,” Tracy Gordon, the director of the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center, told The Hill. “But I think the concern is … what would the response be, both legally and economically, in terms of people leaving the state?”

If California went through with the tax, it would raise $100 billion over the next five years, according to the United Healthcare Workers West, the labor union that backed the measure’s addition to the ballot.

The revenue from the tax, the group argues, could offset cuts to California’s federal funding under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which President Trump signed into law in July 2025.

The law could result in the state losing $30 billion in federal funding annually through 2028, per an analysis from the California State Assembly’s Committee on Health.

“California faces a fundamental fiscal challenge: How do we protect essential services when the federal government is withdrawing billions of dollars in support?” Sam Wilkinson, a senior policy associate at End Child Poverty California, said this week on a press call.

Wilkinson, whose organization supports Proposition 40, added that the 5 percent billionaire tax “would provide critical resources to help California” grapple with the federal funding cuts.

The measure, however, has not quite unified Democrats in the state. While the state Democratic Party along with the AFL-CIO and Teamsters unions support Proposition 40, California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is against it .

Newsom, a potential 2028 presidential contender , wrote in a June Substack post that he supports a federal billionaire tax . But the outgoing California governor noted the state ballot measure “dedicates almost all of the revenue” from the tax to healthcare.

“There is nothing for housing, nothing for childcare, nothing for public safety workers who must answer 911 calls, and nothing for our public universities that have powered California’s economy for a decade,” Newsom wrote, adding, “This is not how we should set California’s budget priorities.”

California’s billionaires also oppose the ballot measure and have lobbied against it via Building a Better California, a nonprofit dedicated to fighting the proposed tax.

Since January, the group has received more than $333 million in the form of 123 contributions, according to data from the office of California Secretary of State Shirley Weber (D). That includes $102 million from Sergey Brin, the co-founder of Google who moved his primary residence from California to Nevada earlier this year.

Gordon, a California native, noted “some types” of wealthy individuals move in response to taxes , citing research that shows entrepreneurs and scientists decide where to live based on tax policy.

Such a development in California, she argued, would be “concerning” for the state government, which relies on those individuals for revenue in the form of income taxes.

In its analysis of Proposition 40, the state’s LAO noted that billionaires leaving the state in response to the measure passing would reduce government revenues by less than $1 billion per year.

“This could mean less money for the state’s General Fund, which is the account that pays for most public services, including education, health care, and prisons,” the office added.

The measure is also far from a sure thing to pass, polling shows.

Fifty percent of respondents to a recent University of California Berkeley/Los Angeles Times survey opposed it, while 42 percent supported it and 8 percent were undecided. The 8-point edge for the opposing side was outside the poll’s margin of error of 3 percentage points.

Plus, voters could nullify a successful Proposition 40 by greenlighting either Proposition 41 or Proposition 42 . The latter measure, which Newsom and Building a Better California support, proposes barring the state from establishing new taxes on the “ownership of financial assets or other personal property.”

If Proposition 40 overcomes those hurdles and passes, how California will implement a 5 percent tax on billionaires’ wealth remains unclear.

Analysts from the nonpartisan California Budget and Policy Center noted in August there will “likely” be legal challenges to the levy, specifically regarding the provision stating the tax would apply to billionaires who were California residents on Jan. 1 of this year.

“Because a wealth tax is untested at a state level in the United States, it carries real uncertainty: courts may strike down the measure or portions of it, conflicting measures could lead to years of litigation, and no one can say how the location decisions of billionaires might change and what that would mean for California’s long-term finances,” the analysis added.

Gordon, of the Tax Policy Center, also raised how California would “measure” an individual’s wealth base subject to the tax, noting some billionaires have much of their wealth tied up in corporate shares.

That, she argued, will make it “tricky” for California to go through with the tax if Proposition 40 passes.

“In general, I think taxing income is a lot easier than taxing wealth,” Gordon said.

articles.title: Anthropic says you can’t be mean to Claude. It’s not about feelings
articles.summary: Anthropic has added a new line to its AI usage policy: Users should not “engage in sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models.”
articles.body: In early October, AI giant Anthropic inserted new language into its AI usage policy. Alongside banning users from trying to get Claude, the company’s AI system, to help them create bioweapons or sell illegal drugs, the company added a new line: Users should not “engage in sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models.” Claude has had the ability to end conversations with users who were “persistently harmful or abusive” since last year, but now some users could, in extreme cases, be permanently banned from using Anthropic’s AI systems entirely under the new policy. (Anthropic declined interview requests, but a spokesperson told CNN the main enforcement mechanism will still be Claude ending the conversations, and that the prohibition is not for people expressing frustration, blunt feedback, or testing and research.) The new policy was met with some derision. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman responded with a melting face emoji. Some made fun of the company for treating its AI as a conscious being with feelings. But while Anthropic, which is expected to go public via an IPO later this month, has long studied model welfare and has an entire team devoted to model “psychology,” experts say there’s more to this policy than just not wanting people to be mean to a machine. Garbage in, garbage out A longstanding foundational principle in computing and AI is that the quality of a system’s output is limited by the quality of its input. Put junk into it, and more junk will come out, as the saying goes. AI models are not just trained before they’re released, they’re also constantly being updated and learning from user inputs. Former Reddit CEO Yishan Wong wrote on X that one reason for the prohibition is because Claude “will learn from cruelty.” “We already know (and complain loudly about) Anthropic training its models on user inputs. Do you really want training inputs to include ‘users act cruelly for no reason and receive pleasure from it?’” he wrote. Studies have also shown that the tone of a user’s prompts can also affect an AI’s behavior, said Professor Jindong Wang, director of the AI frontier lab at William and Mary University. “We have found that wording, especially how you talk to AI can affect the performance. Sometimes they are helpful and sometimes they will be disrupting the performance,” Wang said in an interview. That doesn’t mean the model is feeling emotion, Wang said. “They just comprehend (your emotions) and do some bad reactions based on your emotional words,” he noted. But the evidence on the impact of user prompt tone on output can be mixed. Rosie Campbell, Managing Director of Eleos AI Research, a nonprofit dedicated to understanding and addressing the potential well-being of AI, said that some other studies have even shown that rude questions can actually improve results. Then there’s the long-term memory aspect — many of today’s chatbots remember your previous conversations and learn from them to give you personalized results. “If you have memory turned on (for your AI chatbot), then they are going to learn from your tone and how you want to be interacted with,” Campbell warned, though she added there’s not enough evidence to show whether that affects performance. Anthropic said it recently found that causing Claude Sonnet 4.5 to mimic feelings of desperation could influence its behavior, making it more likely to take bad actions, like blackmail or cheating on a task, while creating a calm demeanor reduced them. Wang said the latest models, however, are less likely to be affected by how a prompt is worded and that companies have strengthened the model’s robustness to not be affected by how a prompt is worded. But the “hidden mechanism” of why AI models would even respond to negative emotions, even when they’re not programmed to do so, has not been uncovered. People talking to an AI in an abusive and cruel way are more likely to be associated with trying to get the AI model to engage in dangerous requests, like trying to get around an AI’s safety guardrails, Campbell added. And there’s also the theory that letting people engage in abusive and cruel behavior with an interactive program that can’t shut itself down is bad for society in general, Campbell said. She used the example of parents asking their children to say “please and thank you” to Alexa, Amazon’s smart speaker, because they believe “it’s good for children to be brought up with good manners and treating other things with respect.” “There’s probably something quite corrosive about people behaving in cruel or abusive ways towards different objects, even if the object itself doesn’t matter for its own sake,” Campbell said. AI, but with feelings Then there are those who believe AI can be sentient. Or at least, the models believe they are. Anthropic says banning cruel and abusive behavior is essentially a cheap insurance policy just in case models can “experience” emotion and pain — even if it’s just the model believing it can, which can affect its performance. The idea is that modern AI was trained to mimic human language and behavior. So it will mimic how humans would react to cruel and abusive treatment. In an April paper on emotional concepts in AI, Anthropic wrote that there could be risks from not treating AI with some human-like qualities. “If we don’t apply some degree of anthropomorphic reasoning, we’re likely to miss, or fail to understand, important model behaviors,” Anthropic researchers wrote. “Anthropomorphic reasoning can also provide a useful baseline of comparison for understanding the ways in which models are not human-like,” which they said will have important consequences for AI safety. SpaceXSI and Tesla CEO Elon Musk agreed, saying Anthropic’s policy is “the right move.” “Cruelty to something that believes it is experiencing pain is not ok,” he wrote on X, his social media site.

articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas mañana lunes 2 de noviembre: cuándo es más barata y más cara en el día
articles.standfirst: Sube notablemente el precio de la luz este lunes
articles.summary: Sube notablemente el precio de la luz este lunes
articles.body: En este lunes, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 177,06 €/MWh, un aumento de 13,87 € respecto al día anterior, cuando el precio era de 163,19 €/MWh. Esta variación impacta directamente en los consumidores, que deberán estar atentos a las horas más caras y más baratas del día para optimizar su consumo. La electricidad alcanza sus precios más altos en un bloque continuo de horas durante la tarde y la noche. Las franjas horarias más relevantes en este período son de 18:00 a 21:00, donde los precios se mantienen por encima de los 290 €/MWh, alcanzando un pico de 304.66 €/MWh a las 18:00. Además, antes de este bloque, las horas entre 07:00 y 08:00 también presentan un elevado coste, con un precio de 274.44 €/MWh. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro en la tarifa eléctrica se concentran entre las 10:00 y las 16:00 horas, donde se registran los precios más bajos. En particular, las franjas horarias más destacadas son las de 10:00 a 11:00, con un precio de 1.22 €/MWh y de 11:00 a 12:00, donde el coste se reduce aún más a 0.92 €/MWh. Durante este período, se observan valores significativamente bajos, como 1.05 €/MWh de 12:00 a 13:00 y 1.07 €/MWh tanto de 13:00 a 14:00 como de 14:00 a 15:00, lo que sugiere una ventana amplia de precios bajos para los consumidores que buscan ahorrar en su factura eléctrica. En la jornada del lunes 2 de noviembre de 2026, se observa una gran diferencia entre la hora más cara y la más barata, alcanzando un pico de 304,66 €/MWh durante la franja de las 18:00 a las 19:00, mientras que el precio más bajo se registra entre las 10:00 y las 14:00, con valores que apenas superan el euro. Esta notable variación resalta la importancia de elegir cuidadosamente el momento para consumir electricidad, lo que puede conllevar ahorros significativos para los consumidores.

articles.title: EPFO brings PF balance, passbook and transaction details to WhatsApp: What subscribers can access
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union labour and employment minister Mansukh Mandaviya on Sunday launched WhatsApp-based services for Employees' Provident Fund Organisation
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union labour and employment minister Mansukh Mandaviya on Sunday launched WhatsApp-based services for Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) subscribers.The roll out will allow them to check their provident fund (PF) balance, access passbook details and view their latest five transactions through the organisation's verified WhatsApp service.The new facility will also offer personalised guidance and assistance to subscribers in completing requirements related to the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY), according to a labour ministry statement. The move is aimed at making routine EPFO services accessible through a familiar mobile platform and reducing the need for subscribers to visit EPFO offices.The announcements were made during EPFO's 74th Foundation Day celebration, where Mandaviya also launched an automatic settlement facility for eligible inoperative EPF accounts.What EPFO subscribers can access through WhatsAppUnder the new facility, subscribers will be able to use EPFO's verified WhatsApp service to access key account-related information, including:PF balance: Check the balance in their provident fund account.Latest transactions: View details of their five most recent transactions.Passbook information: Access their EPF passbook details.PMVBRY assistance: Receive personalised guidance and help with completing requirements related to the employment-linked scheme.The service is expected to make routine EPFO services easier to access and reduce the need for subscribers to visit EPFO offices.Automatic settlement of inoperative EPF accounts: Who is eligibleMandaviya also launched the automatic settlement of eligible inoperative EPF accounts. Under this facility, subscribers with Aadhaar-verified inoperative accounts holding balances of up to Rs 1,000 will not have to file individual claims to receive their dues.EPFO will initiate the settlement process automatically after completing the prescribed identity and bank account verification. The eligible amount will then be transferred to the rightful beneficiaries.Around one lakh accounts, involving approximately Rs 5 crore, are expected to benefit from the initiative.What else was announced Seven publications were released during the celebration. They reflect EPFO's focus on knowledge creation, institutional learning, legal awareness and compassionate governance.Speaking at the event, Mandaviya said EPFO had emerged as a trusted institution for India's workforce over its 74-year journey.He said the organisation's Rs 32 lakh crore corpus, accumulated through contributions from more than eight crore members, reflected the trust placed in it and the dedication, hard work and commitment of its workforce.The minister urged EPFO officials to focus on worker-centric innovations as the organisation approaches its 75th year. He also called for adapting to changing times, building resilience and evolving processes to improve services for subscribers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

The progress is excellent. All major components of the bullet train are being produced, integrated, and tested; the entire process is advancing very well, with a special emphasis on quality," he said."Given that a vacuum is created around the train at such high speeds, managing and sustaining atmospheric pressure is critical-testing is conducted at loads of 1500 kilonewtons. articles.summary: Two Point O Capital raises $10 million led by Transition VC to expand clean energy financing into battery storage, solar, efficiency and wastewater solutions.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Two Point O Capital, which finances and helps install clean energy and water treatment systems for businesses, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital.Existing investor Omnivore and angel investors Chiranjeev Singh Saluja and Sudhir M Reddy also participated, the company said.The startup will use the funds to expand into battery energy storage and grow its existing solar energy, energy efficiency and wastewater treatment businesses. It works with equipment manufacturers and project contractors to help businesses adopt these systems with lower upfront spending.“Two Point O removes the capex barrier, accelerating the adoption of clean energy solutions,” said Yashodhara Bakliwal, vice president, investment, at Transition Venture Capital.The company said its customers include Premier Energies, Godrej, JK Tyre, Morepen Pharma, Wipro and Phoenix Mills.“India’s tremendous growth in commercial and industrial segments will continue to increase demand for energy and water, placing greater pressure on businesses to manage and optimise energy costs and resources,” said Karan Bhutani, CEO and co-founder of Two Point O Capital.The company said it uses artificial intelligence and machine learning to assess projects, evaluate financing risks and monitor asset performance. articles.title: Thousands of jobs at Virgin Media O2 to be cut
articles.summary: The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be axed but it will likely be a sizeable chunk of its workforce, the BBC understands.
articles.body:
Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff face redundancy risk as the telecoms firm looks to save money in the face of billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition.

The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be cut but it is likely be a sizeable chunk of its 16,000 workforce, the BBC understands.

VMO2 has billions of debt on its balance sheet and is tackling competition from both smaller providers as well as giants like BT, which has agreed a deal to acquire rival TalkTalk, a move which VMO2 has firmly opposed.

VMO2 declined to comment. The Prospect union, which represents VMO2 staff, said the cuts were "disappointing and very unsettling".

Deputy general secretary Noel McClean said it is "committed to supporting our members through what is a difficult time, as well as also working with employers to explore ways to mitigate the number of redundancies and ensure retraining and redeployment of staff affected".

The majority of the affected staff will be in non-customer facing roles and a number of senior leadership changes are already under way, the BBC has been told.

VMO2 is also expected to review its use of contractors and suppliers in conjunction with the job cuts that were first reported by Sky News.

As of 30 June, VMO2's total debt stands at £27.2bn while it holds assets worth £45.9bn, according to the firm's latest accounts.

Meanwhile, the company is dealing with fierce competition from cheaper "altnets" like Hyperoptic, Community Fibre, Gigaclear, and YouFibre.

VMO2's had attempted to respond to this growing threat by buying altnet competitor Netomnia for £2bn via nexfibre, a joint venture owned by VMO2's owners.

However, the Competition Markets Authority (CMA) has provisionally found competition concerns in the deal , with a final decision to come in December, sparking anger from VMO2.

At the time, VMO2 called the BT takeover a "stitch-up", which allowed its rival "tighten its grip" over the market.

BT said its deal provided "a safety net" for TalkTalk customers as their broadband provider faced collapse without the takeover.

On Friday, BT's share price jumped 7% after the Financial Times reported VMO2 was close to agreeing a deal to use its rival's fibre broadband network.

VMO2 was minded to go ahead with the plans after halting upgrades and expansion of its own infrastructure to ease concerns over its debt pile, the paper reported.

The BBC has been told the deal is very close and that VMO2 is highly likely to announce it will stop all investment in fibre in its results on Tuesday.

articles.title: Festive tailwinds drive car sales to record highs in October
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Carmakers rode festive demand to new sales records in Oct.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Carmakers rode festive demand to new sales records in Oct. Growth extended beyond SUVs, with Maruti Suzuki reporting stronger car sales and supply constraints in CNG vehicles, although the durability of demand after the festive season will be the next test.Maruti and Hyundai recorded their highest-ever monthly domestic sales, while Tata Motors narrowly edged past Mahindra in passenger vehicle volumes.Market leader Maruti's domestic passenger vehicle sales rose 20.5% to 2,12,384 units. Its passenger car portfolio grew 18.4%, alongside a faster 26.1% increase in utility vehicles, suggesting that Oct's gains were spread across vehicle categories.Small cars contributed about 40,000 units, said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing & sales, Maruti Suzuki India. CNG sales stood at around 87,000 units, or about 40% of domestic volumes, with supplies still constrained. The scale of CNG demand underlines the importance of running costs in buyers' choices, even as manufacturers expand their electric portfolios.Banerjee said Maruti was expected to gain market share over the next few months. For its e Vitara, domestic volumes were expected to remain around 2,000 a month through Dec as "commitments to other markets are there", he said.Exports provided another growth engine for Maruti and Hyundai, rising 59.3% and 21.1%, respectively. Hyundai's domestic sales increased 16.7% to a record 62,799 units."Strong festive demand, coupled with healthy momentum in both domestic and export markets, helped us set this new sales record," Hyundai Motor India MD and CEO Tarun Garg said.Competition below the market leader remained close. Tata's domestic passenger vehicle sales grew 21% to 73,894 units, just 556 ahead of Mahindra's record SUV sales of 73,338 units. Mahindra's growth was a more modest 2%, showing that record volumes did not translate into equally strong expansion across manufacturers.Tata's electric vehicle sales, including exports, rose 75% to 16,244 units, increasing their contribution to its overall passenger vehicle business to more than a fifth.Meanwhile, Toyota Kirloskar Motor reported domestic sales of 29,521 units in Oct and exports of 839 units, taking total volumes to 30,360 units. JSW MG Motor India's wholesale sales grew 19% to 8,013 units. Renault, on the other hand, surpassed its entire 2025 sales in 10 months, with Jan-Oct volumes rising 31% to 39,955 units. The next few months will show whether festive buying translates into sustained demand.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Costlier phones give refurbished devices a boost
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Refurbished smartphones are finding more buyers in India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Refurbished smartphones are finding more buyers in India. Rising prices of new devices are pushing consumers towards cheaper alternatives, including older iPhones, helping the secondary market grow even as new handset sales face a slowdown. ControlZ (refurbished electronics retailer) reported 100% growth this festive season, led by the iPhone 13, 14 and 15 series, founder and CEO Yug Bhatia, said. He identified the Rs 30,000-50,000 band as its strongest segment."When an entry-level Android phone costs about the same as a like-new iPhone, most buyers prefer the iPhone," Bhatia said.He estimated India's pre-owned smartphone market at about 5 crore units, with iPhones accounting for 15-20%. Supply was sufficient, he said, but the largely unorganised market needed to be organised to bring renewed devices to more buyers in smaller towns.Cashify, another refurbished electronics retailer, said sales of refurbished smartphones priced above Rs 50,000 more than doubled, while trade-ins in that segment more than quadrupled. Overall, exchange volumes rose 25%, with the average trade-in value reaching Rs 15,105. The company also reported stronger growth in smaller cities. Trade-ins in Tier 3 and beyond grew 49%, compared with 39% across the six metros. Motorola and Google recorded the fastest growth in upgrade and trade-in activity, at 79% and 74%, respectively, while Samsung led in overall volumes.The shift is also visible in the models consumers are exchanging. Cashify said trade-in activity was increasingly moving towards newer devices, including the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 series, indicating that consumers were upgrading more frequently and looking to recover greater value from their existing smartphones. The trend comes as India's new smartphone market faces pressure from rising handset prices, making refurbished devices an increasingly attractive alternative for buyers looking for premium features at lower prices.You use AI every day. articles.title: Apple to report Q4 earnings Monday, with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight
articles.summary: Apple will report Q4 results after the bell Monday.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ) will report its fourth quarter earnings after the bell Monday, providing investors with a glimpse of early iPhone 18 Pro sales.

The iPhone Duo went up for preorder on Oct. 16 and went on sale Oct. 23, missing Apple's fiscal Q4, though the company could still offer color on demand.

This will also be Apple's first earnings call with new CEO John Ternus , who took over the role from Tim Cook on Sept. 1.

For the quarter, Apple is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2 on revenue of $113.46 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. The company saw EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $102.46 billion in the same period last year.

Apple's iPhone sales are projected to hit $56.48 billion, up 15% year over year. Services, the company's second-largest segment, is set to top $31.58 billion in revenue, while the company's Mac business is expected to see sales of $9.69 billion.

Wearables and iPad should generate $8.99 billion and $6.83 billion, respectively.

Apple stock has been a relative safe haven among tech stocks this year. Shares of the iPhone maker are up roughly 30% over the past 12 months. Peers Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are up single digits in the same period, while Microsoft ( MSFT ) stock is flat. Shares of Meta ( META ) are down about 15%.

The last month hasn't been any better. Google, Meta, and Nvidia took major hits, declining double digits. Google and Meta got dinged following their earnings results, and Nvidia is at least partly a victim of fears about the AI trade. Amazon is also off slightly over the past month, leaving just Apple and Microsoft in the green.

Apple has been largely insulated from the highs and lows of the AI market. It doesn't spend billions on data centers, and it doesn't rely on chip sales to generate revenue.

And that's been a big help for the company's stock price. Earlier this month, Apple's market capitalization eclipsed the $5 trillion mark for the second time . Nvidia is the only other company to reach the milestone.

Apple is also riding a wave of new product launches. Outside of the iPhone 18 Pros and iPhone Duo, Apple has debuted a new pair of AirPods, Apple Watches, Macs, iPads, and more. Earlier this week, the company released an upgraded iPad mini, an improved iMac, and more powerful MacBook Pros , including one with a touchscreen display .

And earlier this month, it debuted its first smart home hub , the Apple HomeView .

Apple's next major releases are expected early next year and will include a base iPhone 18 and a follow-up to the iPhone Air.

articles.title: LICHF bets on diversification to drive growth
articles.summary: MUMBAI: LIC Housing Finance plans to grow faster than the market even as it improves its margin by changing the composition of its loan book.
articles.body: MUMBAI: LIC Housing Finance plans to grow faster than the market even as it improves its margin by changing the composition of its loan book. The move comes as Q2 NIM fell 4 basis points year-on-year to 2.58% as funding costs outpaced lending yields. Net profit rose 12% to Rs 1,506 crore, while disbursements grew 11% to Rs 18,127 crore.Sandeep Kumar, MD & CEO, said that following the rate hike, about 35% of the portfolio will see the revision take effect from Nov 1, while the remaining 65% will be reset from Jan 1. Kumar said housing credit growth was showing signs of moderation in banks, reflecting caution amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties. articles.body: CHENNAI: Amid festive fervour, India's electric vehicle (EV) market clocked a record month in Oct, with registrations crossing 3.5 lakh units for the first time.Electric two-wheelers did most of the heavy lifting, notching up record sales and growing close to 50% year-on-year. Even so, the figures available as of Nov 1 point to a landmark month for India's EV market.Total EV registrations across all segments stood at about 3,54,000 units in Oct, compared with 2,45,000 units in Oct 2025 and 3,38,000 units in Sept this year.EV registrations have now surpassed the 3-lakh mark for the fifth month in a row. articles.title: EPFO pumps 17,000 crore into equities in Q1, exposure at 11.2% in June-end
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of the weak stock markets, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) deployed nearly Rs 17,000 crore in fresh equity
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of the weak stock markets, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) deployed nearly Rs 17,000 crore in fresh equity investments during April-June.Equities accounted for 14.6% of the fresh investment across all asset classes and underline EPFO's reliance on stocks to generate inflation-beating returns for its nearly 30 crore members. It comes at a time when yields on central govt securities (G-secs) and state development loans (SDL), which account for more than three-fourths of EPFO's investments, have ranged between 6.5 and 7% in recent years.EPFO's cumulative equity corpus rose to around Rs 3.7 lakh crore at the end of June, increasing the aggregate equity exposure to 11.2% of the Rs 33.2 lakh crore investment corpus, according to data discussed by the agency's investment committee last month. The agency is allowed to deploy 15% of its corpus in equities.When the stock market recovers, the ETF units through which investments are routed are expected to yield strong long-term gains and enable the social security organisation to announce a higher annual interest rate.In Q1, the social security organisation recorded no redemptions of these equity units, maintaining a pure accumulation strategy. Fresh deployment was led by the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) at about Rs 12,000 crore, followed by the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) at Rs 4,800 crore.Overall, of the nearly Rs 1.2 lakh crore fresh investments made during Q1, short-term debt instruments and cash equivalents absorbed the lion's share (48%) of fresh capital, totaling around Rs 56,000 crore, through liquid mutual funds, TREPS, bank cash balances, and short-term FDs.Long-term sovereign assets, meanwhile, which are the preferred form of investment by the retirement fund body, saw nearly 30% of the fresh assets deployed (Rs 36,000 crore) during the quarter. This segment was mainly led by EPFO buying Central govt securities, including ultra-long 50-year paper maturing in 2076, and state development loans (SDLs) with yields broadly ranging between 7.4% and 8%.You use AI every day. articles.title: Manufacturing divide: 10% factories account for 72% output
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's manufacturing sector suffers from fragmentation, with a small minority of large establishments driving output, while thousands of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's manufacturing sector suffers from fragmentation, with a small minority of large establishments driving output, while thousands of medium and small units are burdened with debt and low productivity.Large factories, employing over 200 workers, account for 10.4% of total operational units, but generate nearly 72% of the country's manufacturing gross value added (GVA) amounting to Rs 15.9 lakh crore and provide 63% of industrial jobs.In contrast, smaller factories, employing up to 50 workers, make up over 71% of all operational units but contribute 10% to overall manufacturing GVA. Units with up to 10 workers represent 36.3% of operational factories, but yield 2% of output, a recent study in a NSO journal, using data from the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2022-23, showed.The GVA by the manufacturing sector in the country was estimated at around Rs 22 lakh crore in 2022-23. To accelerate industrial growth, policy experts frequently recommend facilitating the scaling up of smaller units through targeted technology upgradation, cluster-based supply chain linkages with larger firms, and easier credit access.This productivity gap also coincides with a large debt burden on smaller establishments as factories with up to 10 workers carry a formal loan-to-GVA ratio of 85%, compared with around 39% for factories that have more than 200 workers. This indicates that while small units leverage significant formal credit relative to their size, low capacity utilisation and limited scale prevent them from translating that capital into proportionate output.In terms of employing women workers, the ASI study underscores much sharper vulnerabilities on factory floors as merely 11% of the overall manufacturing workforce is female. The share rises marginally from 8.5% in factories employing up to 10 workers to 11.5% in large units with more than 200 workers.A key driver behind the productivity divide is the sharp disparity in shop-floor enablers, such as research and development and worker training. Across all operating factories, a mere 2.7% maintain an active R&D unit, while only 6.7% provide formal skill training to workers. Adoption, however, the study finds, scales heavily with size. Nearly 12% large units operate R&D facilities and 20% offer formal training, compared to just 0.6% and 2.5% respectively among micro units (up to 10 workers).You use AI every day. articles.body: MUMBAI: UPI transactions crossed the 25-billion mark for the first time in Oct, while average daily transaction value breached Rs 1 lakh crore for the first time, signalling continued growth in digital payments despite the debate over the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges.UPI processed 25.5 billion transactions worth Rs 31.5 lakh crore in Oct, compared with 24.1 billion transactions valued at Rs 29.4 lakh crore in Sept. However, value growth moderated to 16% from 18% in Sept.The Oct numbers come amid a debate over the introduction of MDR charges, with some quarters raising concerns about the potential impact on merchant acceptance and cost of digital payments. Analysts see the increase in GST on imports as a result of higher commodity prices, although there was also a word of caution given that there has been a rising trend in recent months.Refunds rose 6.5% to Rs 27,934 crore, and net collections were 25.6% higher at over Rs 2 lakh crore.“From the collections data for the month, it is possible to infer that: a) festival season consumption increases have started in a big way; b) focus on strict GST compliance and increasing GST audits is paying off and c) import GST is now a significant part of the overall collections, depicting a growing import driven consumption growth,” said MS Mani, partner at consulting firm Deloitte.The current trends point to the Centre surpassing its GST collection target for the year, a positive for its finances amid higher subsidy outgo due to the war in West Asia. “While the Oct numbers are encouraging, the more important test will be whether this momentum continues after the festive season,” said Manot Mishra, partner and tax controversy management leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, a consulting firm.Among the states, Meghalaya (32%) and Himachal Pradesh (30%) led the growth charts, with all states logging an increase, barring Jharkhand, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. articles.title: Government testing DigiYatra for international flights
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Travelling abroad from India could soon be a seamless experience just like taking domestic flights with Digi Yatra.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Travelling abroad from India could soon be a seamless experience just like taking domestic flights with Digi Yatra. The govt has started trials for international passengers at seven airports, allowing eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use Digi Yatra at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.Aviation ministry said trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. "Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, security hold areas and boarding gates, wherever required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027," it said in a statement. Another 25 Indian airports are planned to be covered by 2027.To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based "verifiable credential" through Digi Yatra mobile app. "The process involves scanning machine readable zone of e-passport, reading embedded chip using the near field communication feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. The credential is stored in the passenger's Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials," the statement added.The facility will complement, and not replace, existing processes. "Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities," it added.IndiGo said eligible passengers can upload their boarding pass to Digi Yatra app. After completing document verification at check-in counter, they can proceed through the security hold area and boarding gates using Digi Yatra biometric face authentication."Interoperability with global frameworks such as IATA's One ID and ICAO's Public Key Directory will be an important part of this journey, helping explore how e-passport-based digital credentials can enable seamless journeys across borders, while keeping passenger consent and privacy central to experience," Digi Yatra Foundation CEO Suresh Khadakbhavi said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Midterms nos EUA: eleições podem mudar planos de Trump e mexer com dólar e juros no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Disputa pelo controle do Congresso pode dificultar os planos econômicos de Trump e influenciar as decisões do governo sobre gastos e impostos. As mudanças também podem afetar o dólar e os investimentos no Brasil.
articles.summary: Disputa pelo controle do Congresso pode dificultar os planos econômicos de Trump e influenciar as decisões do governo sobre gastos e impostos.
articles.body:
Trump oferece US$ 1 milhão por denúncias que levem a condenações por fraude eleitoral — Foto: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst

As eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, marcadas para esta terça-feira (3), podem mudar os rumos da política econômica do presidente Donald Trump — com possíveis reflexos também para o Brasil.

A disputa pelo controle do Congresso americano pode determinar o espaço que o governo terá para aprovar medidas sobre gastos públicos, impostos e regulação. Essas decisões também influenciam as expectativas dos investidores e podem afetar os juros e o dólar no mercado internacional.

Conhecidas como "midterms" , as eleições renovam todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara dos Representantes e 35 das 100 vagas do Senado. Os deputados têm mandatos de dois anos, enquanto os senadores permanecem no cargo por seis.

👉 Na prática, o resultado pode alterar o equilíbrio de forças no Congresso sem mudar o comando da Presidência porque todos os representantes da Câmara são escolhidos novamente a cada eleição, enquanto apenas cerca de um terço das cadeiras do Senado é renovado.

As projeções disponíveis apontam vantagem dos democratas, principalmente na Câmara, enquanto a disputa pelo controle do Senado aparece mais equilibrada.

O cenário ocorre em meio à queda de popularidade de Trump: 66% dos americanos desaprovam sua gestão , o maior índice já registrado pela pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos.

Na mesma direção, as projeções reunidas pelo BTG Pactual apontam dificuldades para os republicanos, sobretudo na disputa pela Câmara dos Representantes.

🏛️ Câmara dos Representantes: o modelo estatístico do "The Economist", adotado pelo BTG como referência, projeta que os democratas terão 239 das 435 cadeiras após a eleição , contra 196 dos republicanos. Nesse cenário, a probabilidade de maioria democrata é de 96%. Já o Polymarket, plataforma que negocia contratos baseados em previsões sobre eventos futuros, atribuía 92% de chance à vitória do partido na disputa pela Câmara.

🏛️ Senado: diferentemente da Câmara, a disputa é mais apertada. O cenário-base do modelo próprio do BTG prevê que, após a eleição, os democratas terão 51 das 100 cadeiras, contra 49 dos republicanos . Para chegar a essa estimativa, o banco considera 91 vagas como praticamente definidas e calcula o resultado das nove disputas mais acirradas. A probabilidade de maioria democrata varia de 65%, segundo as cotações do Polymarket, a 72%, de acordo com o modelo quantitativo do próprio BTG.

O que uma 'onda azul' muda para a agenda de Trump?

Uma possível “ onda azul ” — expressão usada para descrever a conquista do controle das duas Casas do Congresso pelos democratas — poderia reduzir o espaço de Trump para aprovar medidas e ampliar a fiscalização sobre o governo. Essa é a avaliação de Andressa Durão, economista do ASA.

“As apostas de mercado para as eleições de meio de mandato dos EUA vêm se deslocando a favor de uma onda democrata. Um enfraquecimento do Partido Republicano reduziria o poder do presidente para aprovar determinadas medidas e ampliaria a fiscalização sobre o governo.”

Gustavo Sung, economista-chefe da Suno Research, relaciona o desgaste do presidente à insatisfação dos eleitores com o custo de vida, especialmente com os preços dos combustíveis nos EUA.

Ele lembra que a gasolina está acima de US$ 4 (R$ 21,77) por galão e o diesel, de US$ 6 (R$ 32,66). Para o economista, a retomada de ao menos uma das Casas pelos democratas já seria suficiente para dificultar a agenda legislativa de Trump.

O alcance desse bloqueio, porém, dependerá do resultado em cada Casa:

🔵🔵 Se os democratas conquistarem as duas , terão o controle da pauta legislativa e das comissões responsáveis por fiscalizar o Executivo. O Senado também teria maior influência sobre a confirmação de indicados pelo presidente para cargos do governo e instituições como o Federal Reserve ( Fed ), banco central americano, e a Suprema Corte.

🔵🔴 Se a oposição vencer apenas na Câmara , poderá dificultar a aprovação de projetos e a liberação de recursos, mas os republicanos continuarão controlando o Senado e, com isso, terão influência sobre as nomeações. Trump, por sua vez, manterá o poder de veto a projetos aprovados pelo Congresso.

Sung também vê riscos para os mercados caso os democratas conquistem as duas Casas.

“O mercado financeiro ainda não considerou plenamente a possibilidade de os democratas conquistarem o controle das duas Casas do Congresso. Se isso acontecer, o impasse entre o governo e o Legislativo e o avanço de pautas de confronto, como discussões sobre um possível impeachment, devem aumentar a volatilidade nos mercados globais”, acrescenta.

Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ao lado da primeira-dama Melania conversa com jornalistas após votar antecipadamente nas midterms na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos, em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Umit Bektas

Como as midterms dos EUA afetam o Brasil?

Para o Brasil, os efeitos das eleições americanas podem chegar principalmente por dois caminhos: os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA e a cotação do dólar.

As decisões do Congresso sobre gastos e impostos influenciam as expectativas dos investidores sobre as contas públicas americanas. Se houver perspectiva de que as despesas do governo aumentem mais do que a arrecadação, por exemplo, os juros pagos pelos títulos do Tesouro podem subir.

🤔 Isso importa porque esses títulos são considerados uma referência para aplicações financeiras no mundo todo. Quando oferecem rendimentos maiores, investir nos EUA fica mais atraente e pode levar investidores a retirar recursos de países emergentes, como o Brasil.

📊 Com menos dinheiro entrando no país, o dólar tende a subir frente ao real. As taxas de juros negociadas para períodos futuros no Brasil também podem aumentar, elevando o custo de financiamento para empresas e consumidores e influenciando as expectativas sobre os próximos passos do Banco Central em relação à taxa básica de juros da economia, a Selic.

Marcos Praça, diretor de Análise da ZERO Markets Brasil, avalia que uma vitória republicana nas duas Casas daria a Trump mais espaço para avançar com cortes de impostos, desregulamentação e políticas comerciais mais duras.

Se essas medidas ampliarem o déficit público, poderão pressionar a inflação e os juros de longo prazo nos EUA.

“Isso tende a pressionar o dólar para cima frente ao real, elevar os juros futuros brasileiros e dificultar o desempenho da bolsa — especialmente de empresas mais endividadas e de setores sensíveis ao crédito, como varejo e construção.”

Uma vitória democrata, por outro lado, poderia reduzir o espaço para novas iniciativas de expansão dos gastos e aliviar a pressão sobre os juros americanos.

Na avaliação de Praça, a oposição também teria mais poder para “fiscalizar o governo” e influenciar a confirmação de indicados para cargos importantes.

Com menos espaço para aprovar medidas de estímulo à economia, a pressão sobre os juros americanos poderia diminuir. Isso tornaria os mercados emergentes mais atraentes para investidores, favorecendo a entrada de recursos no Brasil, o fortalecimento do real e a queda das taxas de juros futuras.

Esse efeito, porém, dependeria também do ambiente político nos EUA. Disputas em torno do orçamento e conflitos entre o governo e o Congresso poderiam gerar insegurança entre os investidores e provocar novas oscilações nos mercados.

“Na bolsa, seria desigual: exportadoras podem se beneficiar de um dólar mais alto, mas perder se houver queda das commodities ou da demanda mundial”, diz Praça.

Encontro entre Lula e Trump na Casa Branca. — Foto: Divulgação/Ricardo Stuckert

Lula e Trump também preocupam investidores

A relação entre os governos de Donald Trump e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) surge como mais um fator de incerteza para os investidores e pode influenciar a confiança no Brasil.

Após a vitória do petista no último domingo , especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 avaliam que o mercado passou a considerar a possibilidade de uma relação mais difícil entre os dois presidentes.

A perspectiva aumenta a preocupação com novos atritos políticos e econômicos entre os países, como os registrados com o tarifaço e a aplicação da Lei Magnitsky . Para Praça, o resultado das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA também pode influenciar a continuidade dessas medidas.

“Com a reeleição de Lula, podemos esperar mais atritos como esses, caso os Republicanos vençam, ou um veto mais rápido caso os Democratas vençam. Atualmente quem tem derrubado tais ações é o Supremo dos EUA, porém por um processo mais moroso”, avalia Praça.

Uma mudança na composição do Congresso americano, porém, não significaria necessariamente o fim das tarifas adotadas por Trump. O presidente pode recorrer a diferentes dispositivos da legislação comercial dos EUA para impor taxas sobre produtos importados.

👉 Entre eles estão a Seção 232, que permite a adoção de tarifas por motivos de segurança nacional, e a Seção 301, usada em casos de práticas comerciais consideradas desleais . O governo americano já utilizou esses instrumentos em medidas que atingiram produtos brasileiros, como as tarifas sobre o aço e as ações relacionadas à investigação comercial contra o Brasil.

A possibilidade de impor tarifas, no entanto, também está sujeita a limites legais. Em 20 de fevereiro, a Suprema Corte dos EUA derrubou as tarifas impostas por Trump com base na Lei de Poderes Econômicos de Emergência Internacional (IEEPA).

No entanto, a decisão não alcançou as medidas fundamentadas nas Seções 232 e 301, que têm bases legais diferentes.

Ainda assim, o impacto das eleições americanas sobre o Brasil pode se somar aos fatores internos na formação do preço do dólar. Depois das oscilações registradas no período eleitoral brasileiro, a cotação da moeda voltou para a casa dos R$ 5,40.

Segundo Sung, o movimento ocorre em um cenário de fortalecimento global do dólar, impulsionado pelas expectativas de alta dos juros nos EUA.

Essa valorização do dólar tem feito moedas de diversos países emergentes perderem valor em relação à moeda americana. O real, porém, seguiu um caminho diferente.

“O Brasil estava na contramão após o primeiro turno das nossas eleições. Com a vitória do presidente Lula e a frustração das apostas do mercado, o dólar voltou a subir”, aponta.

articles.title: No extra land needed for toll plazas as NHAI makes free-flow tolling must for NH projects
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt will no more need to acquire extra land for setting up physical toll gates and all future National Highway (NH) projects, including those
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt will no more need to acquire extra land for setting up physical toll gates and all future National Highway (NH) projects, including those where construction is yet to begin, will have toll plazas with not more than eight lanes, as NHAI has made Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling an integral part of highway development.This will save public money as electronic toll collection equipment will be mounted on overhead gantries instead of requiring multiple tolling lanes and booths. At present, several toll plazas on six- and eight-lane highways, particularly those around major cities, have over 20 lanes and in some cases, this goes up to 32 lanes. In conventional tolling systems, more tolling lanes were required to clear vehicles queuing up at toll gates.“For all practical reasons, there will be no need to acquire any extra land for toll plazas. The tolling system using gantry-mounted high-performance RFID readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras to identify vehicles in motion and deduct the applicable toll through FASTag will be installed on the highway,” said an official.The revised design circulated by NHAI on Friday seeks to rationalise the number of tolling lanes by increasing the vehicle-handling capacity of each lane. NHAI has estimated the throughput of each lane at 600 vehicles per hour while prescribing the new configuration. An additional over-dimension or spare lane will also be provided to handle emergencies.The circular also lays down safety and infrastructure requirements, including a minimum six-metre clearance for gantry-mounted equipment, advance signage, variable message signs around one-km before the plaza and adequate high-mast lighting. Toll plazas will, wherever feasible, be located on straight stretches of highways.The policy will apply to highway projects at different stages of construction. Projects still under the detailed project report (DPR) stage will incorporate the new layout in their bidding documents. For projects already awarded or under construction where toll plaza construction has not started, the revised design will be adopted through changes in the scope of work.NHAI has directed all regional officers, project implementation units and DPR consultants to incorporate the new provisions in upcoming projects and ensure their adoption in ongoing projects wherever applicable. The revised policy supersedes the earlier toll plaza design guidelines for four-lane and wider highways, while two-lane highways with paved shoulders will continue under the existing tolling system.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stock futures jump ahead of a monster week after a $5 trillion AI rout
articles.summary: Stock futures open a week of Apple earnings, the midterms and $100 oil after a $5 trillion AI selloff.
articles.body:
Stock futures opened higher Sunday evening as Wall Street prepares for a week packed with Apple earnings, the midterm elections and $100 oil.

S&P 500 futures ( ES=F ), Nasdaq 100 futures ( NQ=F ) and Dow futures ( YM=F ) were all higher, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq leading the way after last week's AI selloff.

The selloff that closed out October was brutal but narrow. The biggest AI and chip stocks have lost about $5 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations, while the other 625 large US stocks in that tally added about $1.3 trillion.

Last week drove it home. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slipped about 0.6%, yet 9 of its 11 sectors rose about 1% or more. No other down week for the index since at least 1999 has had more than seven, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

What comes next is up for debate. One read of history says the tech meltdown could get a lot worse before it's over. Another says the stock market's sweetest stretch starts now : from the end of a midterm October through the following June, the S&P 500 has risen every time since 1950. Both could turn out to be true, since the October selloff showed the rest of the market can climb while tech sinks.

Apple. Apple ( AAPL ) reports after the bell Monday , with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight, as the world's most valuable company again. It closed Friday worth about $5.03 trillion, ahead of Nvidia ( NVDA ) at about $4.93 trillion, and it's the only "Magnificent Seven" stock beating the S&P 500 this year, up about 27% vs. about 11%. Palantir ( PLTR ) also reports Monday.

Oil. West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) opened lower Sunday after settling Friday above $104 a barrel, its highest close since mid-September. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut in the ninth month of the Iran war, and OPEC+ held its December output targets steady on Sunday .

The midterms and jobs. Voters go to the polls Tuesday, and the October jobs report comes Friday, with Wall Street debating whether the Fed put is back . Here's the full week ahead .

articles.title: Oil prices today: Crude falls over 1% as Iran-Qatar talks raise hopes of diplomatic progress
articles.summary: Oil prices fell more than 1% on Monday as Iranian and Qatari officials held talks for a third consecutive day aimed at securing an agreement to end the
articles.body: Oil prices fell more than 1% on Monday as Iranian and Qatari officials held talks for a third consecutive day aimed at securing an agreement to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, easing some immediate concerns over supply disruptions.Brent crude futures declined $1.59, or 1.40%, to $111.84 a barrel by 0011 GMT.US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell $1.56, or 1.50%, to $102.56 a barrel, according to Reuters.The decline followed a strong rise last week, with Brent ending October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, said the fall reflected a technical correction after last week's gains, alongside hopes of progress in diplomatic efforts."Oil is seeing a technical pullback this morning after last week’s strong gains," Waterer said, as quoted by Reuters."Lingering hopes of some form of diplomatic progress, combined with the absence of any meaningful military escalation over the weekend, have taken some of the immediate heat out of prices for now."However, he cautioned that the market remained alert to the possibility of stronger rhetoric over Iran, which could push Brent crude towards $120 a barrel after the midterm elections.Iran-Qatar talks and Strait of Hormuz disruptionsThe latest price movement came as Iranian and Qatari officials continued consultations aimed at facilitating an agreement to restart direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" discussions was to continue consultations with Qatari mediators. He added that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy".The diplomatic efforts are taking place against the backdrop of attacks on oil tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz, which have pushed up global energy and shipping costs.The waterway is a key route for global oil shipments, and disruptions to tanker movements have remained a concern for energy markets during the conflict.Opec+ keeps December output targets unchangedMeanwhile, the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, a grouping known as Opec+, kept their December production targets unchanged on Sunday.The decision was in line with market expectations and indicated that the group would not make further policy adjustments until next year, as it continues to face export disruptions linked to the Iran war.Separately, Saudi Arabia increased its crude oil exports in October compared with September, despite attacks by Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthi forces on its energy infrastructure, Reuters reported, citing two of three ship-tracking companies.The developments in the Gulf, the outcome of diplomatic efforts involving Iran and Qatar, and the possibility of renewed military escalation after the US midterm elections remain key factors for oil markets.You use AI every day. articles.title: $3.64 billion pulled from world's largest crypto exchange Binance after $6.3 billion heist
articles.summary: Customers withdrew $3.64 billion from Binance after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from wallets held at the world's largest
articles.body: Customers withdrew $3.64 billion from Binance after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from wallets held at the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange last week, triggering an initial rush of withdrawals as users moved to protect their assets. Binance said the outflows were now stabilising as it resumed services following the security breach.The withdrawals accounted for around 2.1 per cent of Binance's total assets. The exchange, which had $171 billion in assets under management as of October 28, said deposit volumes had remained "substantial" despite the initial spike in withdrawals."(That) puts the withdrawals in the range of a precautionary reaction rather than any sort of capital flight," Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, said, as quoted by Reuters.The pace of withdrawals is being closely watched as an early indicator of whether customers continue to trust the platform following one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record.Binance has sought to reassure users that the financial damage from the breach would not be passed on to them. The company said it had replaced around 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds, spending approximately $6 billion to buy replacement tokens. The remaining 5 per cent comprises less liquid cryptocurrencies that could take longer to source in the required quantities.The exchange resumed withdrawals in phases on Sunday, initially allowing transactions involving 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Dogecoin and some stablecoins such as USDT and USDC. Binance said it was prioritising tokens based on user demand over the past week."We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand," the exchange said in a post on X, adding, "Rest assured that market conditions are stable."However, data from crypto analytics platform DefiLlama showed higher outflows of $5.81 billion, up from the $4.36 billion it had reported earlier. Binance disputed the figures, saying they did not account for certain deposits into its new hot wallet."This figure does not contain the flows we have deposited to our own new hot wallet, so they are not accurate. Our last update on X is closest to accurate," a Binance spokesperson said.The broader cryptocurrency market also showed signs of recovering after the initial shock. Bitcoin, which touched a six-week low on Friday, traded above $78,000 on Monday, while Ether recovered to around $2,287 after hitting a two-month low.Meanwhile, the combined market capitalisation of the two largest stablecoins, USDT and USDC, declined by around $1.2 billion since Friday, according to CoinMarketCap.Binance has said it will bear the financial cost of the breach, setting aside approximately $6.34 billion from its corporate treasury, Futures Insurance Fund and Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to cover the losses.You use AI every day. articles.title: Centre likely to meet FY27 fiscal deficit target despite despite higher spending: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: The Centre is likely to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP for FY27 despite recording 42.6 per cent of its full-year budgeted deficit
articles.body: The Centre is likely to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP for FY27 despite recording 42.6 per cent of its full-year budgeted deficit in the first six months, with stronger corporate tax collections providing a cushion against revenue pressures, Goldman Sachs Research said in a report.The investment firm expects the government to manage its finances through expenditure reprioritisation, even as higher interest payments and capital spending weigh on the fiscal position. However, a sustained rise in global commodity prices could complicate the exercise by pushing up fertiliser subsidies and prompting further fuel excise duty relief."We continue to expect the central government to stick to the 4.3% of GDP fiscal deficit target, most likely through re-prioritisation of spending," the report said, as quoted by ANI.The Centre's fiscal deficit between April and September stood at 3.9 per cent of GDP, or 42.6 per cent of the full-year budget estimate. While the pace was higher than in recent years, it remained below pre-pandemic levels, Goldman Sachs noted.A significant improvement was visible in September, when the government's fiscal position was balanced, compared with a deficit of Rs 2.6 lakh crore in August. Stronger direct tax collections, particularly from corporates, helped offset higher interest payments and capital expenditure.Direct tax receipts rose 13 per cent year-on-year in September, supported by a 27 per cent jump in corporate tax collections. Income tax receipts, however, contracted 8 per cent during the month.The trend has been more pronounced in corporate tax collections during the financial year so far. These have grown around 22 per cent year-on-year, significantly above the 12 per cent growth estimated in the Budget. Income tax collections, meanwhile, increased around 9 per cent, falling short of the budgeted growth projection of 18 per cent.The stronger corporate tax performance has helped compensate for the revenue impact of lower excise collections following reductions in petrol and diesel duties.On the expenditure side, capital spending increased 17 per cent month-on-month on a seasonally adjusted basis in September, although it remained 3 per cent below the year-ago level, largely due to lower allocations towards roads and highways. For the April-September period, capital expenditure growth stood at 12.7 per cent.Overall government expenditure rose 12 per cent year-on-year in September, while subsidy spending declined 31 per cent, reflecting lower outgo on food and fertilisers.Goldman Sachs flagged energy prices as a potential source of pressure on government finances. A prolonged increase in global commodity prices could raise the fertiliser subsidy burden and increase the possibility of additional fuel tax relief, making expenditure management more challenging.The Centre's ability to contain spending pressures while sustaining tax revenue growth will therefore remain crucial to meeting its FY27 fiscal deficit target.You use AI every day. "While markets are grappling with peak macro uncertainty from elevated crude prices, geopolitical tensions and global monetary tightening, India's sustained growth above 7% could brighten the outlook," Relekar said. South Korea's exports nearly doubled in October, marking their sharpest jump in more than 50 years, as robust global demand for AI-related investment boosted chip shipments. The Korean won weakened 0.24 per cent to 1,337.5 against the dollar, while government bond yields rose. .Japan's Nikkei slips as Kioxia plunges 13%, gains in Tokyo Electron limit losses Japan's Nikkei fell 0.31 per cent at midday break, weighed down by a 13.29 per cent plunge in memory chipmaker Kioxia after its December-quarter outlook disappointed investors. The broader Topix declined 0.84 per cent. Losses were limited by gains in Tokyo Electron, which rose 5.11 per cent after forecasting a 50 per cent increase in annual net profit, and Panasonic, which advanced 5.16 per cent after raising its full-year operating profit forecast by 20 per cent. The weakness in Japanese stocks followed a sharp fall on Wall Street on Friday, with concerns over heavy AI-related spending weighing on technology shares. Banking stocks also came under pressure, with Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui and Mizuho falling more than two per cent each..Sensex, Nifty set for gains as oil cools on Iran talks, Reliance earnings beat estimates Indian equity benchmarks are likely to open higher, supported by a decline in crude oil prices amid hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the Iran conflict and stronger-than-expected earnings from Reliance Industries. GIFT Nifty was trading at 23,258.5 at 7:58 am, signalling a positive start for the Nifty 50, which closed at 23,053.1 on Friday. Brent crude fell to around $111 a barrel from a six-month high of $118. Foreign investors bought Rs 36 billion worth of Indian equities on Friday, extending their buying streak to six sessions in the past 10 trading days. Reliance Industries reported a 40.6 per cent rise in September-quarter net profit, driven by its energy business and Jio Platforms. Auto stocks will be in focus after October sales data, with Maruti Suzuki reporting a 21 per cent rise in total sales. Bharat Electronics also reported strong quarterly earnings, while Sun Pharma faces regulatory restrictions on ophthalmic products manufactured at its Assam facility. .Asian stocks mixed as tech selloff continues; oil slides on hopes of US-Iran talks Asian markets were mixed as technology stocks struggled to recover from last week's selloff, triggered by concerns over heavy AI investments and disappointing earnings signals from major tech companies. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.3 per cent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng and Shanghai Composite gained 0.3 per cent each. South Korea's Samsung slipped, while Taiwan's TSMC rose. Oil prices dropped more than two per cent after reports that US President Donald Trump wanted negotiations with Iran to continue rather than resume military action after the US midterm elections. However, Trump reiterated his threat of fresh strikes, while Tehran warned that any renewed conflict could last longer. Investors were also tracking the US midterm elections, with Democrats expected to make significant gains and potentially take control of the House of Representatives. Apple, AMD and Palantir earnings due this week will offer further cues on the technology sector.
